Implement connection tests that send only synthetic input.
Implement route resolution with fallbacks and the egress decision function every model or provider call must pass.
Implement caps with a hard stop and kill switches with two-person release.

Scope model routes by job (task class) and optionally by agent module or extension, resolve the most specific active route (extension, then module, then job) and refuse a call without one; active routes name a pinned provider revision (ADR 010 decision 25).
Store versioned cost records per model (ModelPricingSchema with basis and observation date); a cost record feeds margins and dashboards and never changes a participant's sale price.

Record processing country and residency on every connection; refuse connections hosted in a restricted place; audit every connection, route, egress, cap and kill-switch change with actor, reason and before and after values.
acceptance: No API response, log line, audit event or outbox payload contains a secret value (tested by scanning).
A call with a non-public data class to a connection without an allow rule is refused.
An exhausted cap blocks new paid calls.
Route resolution picks extension, then module, then job, and a call without an active route is refused (tested).
A route that may carry a non-public data class cannot be activated by its drafter alone, and a connection hosted in a restricted place cannot be saved (negative tests).
A new cost record leaves every active sale price unchanged (test).

packages.title: Jurisdiction gate and holds: restricted visitors refused at the web proxy and the API, sightings hold the person
packages.goal: Refuse every request from a restricted place at every door with kind words in every language, and hold a signed-in person seen there until a compliance reviewer clears the hold (ADR 014 decisions 2 and 6 to 9; Contribuda parity).
steps: Contracts in packages/contracts/src/sanctions.ts: gate modes, refusal envelope (`jurisdiction.restricted`, `auth.jurisdiction_hold`), hold sources, hold record and clear command; tests.

Pure primitives in packages/contracts/src/sanctions.ts (the web and both backend images ship the contracts package): restricted place from the injected authoritative list, IPv4 and IPv6 parsing (IPv4-mapped IPv6 included), range-table lookup, the `ranges_file`, `edge_header`, `upstream_gate` and `fake` adapters; a generator (packages/compliance/bin) that reduces an operator-supplied city-level CSV to the restricted ranges, region level for Ukraine; no network calls, no dataset shipped.

Web proxy: before anything else, render /restricted in the visitor's language for pages (451 where possible, noindex) and answer 451 for other requests; open doors only for the refusal page, legal pages, health, provider webhooks and unsubscribe; the jurisdiction namespace in all six engine languages; dataset attribution on the page.

API: onRequest hook before principal resolution with the trusted-proxy address; hold the person when a valid session is present; refuse held people on every request and at password, provider and second-factor sign-in with `auth.jurisdiction_hold`; production refuses to start without an explicit gate mode; count refusals per place and day.

Persistence in packages/data/migrations/jurisdiction: jurisdiction_hold (one open hold per person, never deleted, clear columns whole), jurisdiction_refusal_count, a SECURITY DEFINER clear command authorized through admin_authorize with permission admin.screening.holds.clear, never by the subject, audited with admin_record; real-PostgreSQL negative and concurrency tests.
acceptance: A request from a restricted place is refused by the web proxy and by the API alike, including a path the proxy does not know (tested with the fake adapter and documentation address ranges).
A refused request with a valid session holds the person; concurrent sightings leave exactly one open hold (tested on PostgreSQL).

A held person is refused on every request and at every sign-in path, and cannot clear their own hold; a reviewer without the permission or without an elevation is refused (tested under the runtime role).
No network address is written to any table, log line or outbox payload (scan and test).
The API refuses to start in production without an explicit gate mode; the `fake` adapter is refused in production.
Every string of the refusal page and the sign-in refusal exists in every engine language.

packages.title: Sanctions list ingestion and freshness through the worker
packages.goal: Keep the baseline OFAC lists and each hub's additional lists as immutable, fresh list versions ingested by the worker, with normalized name keys, so screening never runs against a missing, truncated or stale list (ADR 014 decisions 10 and 11).
steps: Extend the sanctions contracts with list, list version, entry and freshness shapes; name normalization in packages/compliance/src/names (case, marks, punctuation, ICAO 9303 Cyrillic and further script tables as sourced data, sorted distinct tokens).

Parsers in packages/compliance/src/lists for the OFAC Sanctions List Service exports (SDN and consolidated non-SDN, primary names and aliases, entry type, programs, published date) and a fake list with synthetic entries; adapters for additional lists named by country-pack sanctions facts register in ENGINE_ADAPTERS.

Worker jobs (apps/worker/src/screening-lists): `file` mode reads official exports from the data directory, `live` mode is wired but refuses without a provider activated by a second person (KEYS-001), `fake` for tests; stage, check sanity bounds (entry-count drop), activate, emit `screening.list_version_activated`.
Freshness: cadence, warning and stale ages per list; a stale baseline marks screening unavailable; a monthly check of the geolocation range table age with an operations warning past two months.
Persistence in packages/data/migrations/screening-lists: screening_list, screening_list_version (immutable once staged, one active per list), screening_list_entry; baseline rows cannot be paused.
acceptance: A truncated or malformed export is never activated and the previous version stays active (tested).
The baseline lists cannot be paused or deleted by the runtime role or a console path (tested).

Normalization maps the same name written in Latin with marks, in another order or in Cyrillic to the same key (tested with synthetic names, never real listed people in fixtures beyond the published list format).
No network call happens in tests or without an activated live provider.
A list past its stale age is reported stale and makes `screening_available` false (clock test).

packages.title: Screening engine: persons and companies at registration, sign-in and change, matching, results and review cases
packages.goal: Screen every person and company against the active lists with the deterministic engine rule and an optional fuzzy layer, record honest outcomes, open review cases with separation of duties, and expose the screening state other modules gate on (ADR 014 decisions 11 to 15).
steps: Matcher in packages/compliance/src/matching: persons against individuals, companies against entities, the engine rule (all tokens with at most one more on the entry side, or the entry equals the subject minus one token for three or more tokens), `insufficient_name` for one-token names, an optional token-similarity layer within bounds that only adds matches; matcher version in every result.

Worker screening jobs (apps/worker/src/screening) from `identity.person_registered`, `identity.session_started` (only when newer list versions exist or names changed), `company.created` and new name-change events (`identity.name_changed`, `company.renamed`, ownership declaration changes) added minimally in identity and directory; a nightly names-digest sweep as the safety net.

Persistence in packages/data/migrations/screening: screening_subject_state, screening_result, screening_match, screening_decision with guards: decider never the subject or a member of the subject company, no declared conflict, not-same-person and reversals need a second person (register `screening.clear_match` and `screening.reverse_confirmation` as second-person actions with the data integrator's agreement), appeals by a different reviewer; money_held recomputed in the same transaction.

API module apps/api/src/modules/screening: the subject's own status (`core.compliance_status`), the appeal command, staff queue and decision routes under elevation, the internal `screeningState(subject)` port for gates; queue items late after the hub service level; staff notifications that name nobody and cannot be muted.

Confirmed matches suspend the person or company through the existing standing paths, stop their agent and connections, and produce a report draft for the operator; nothing reaches ranking, matching, recommendations or reputation.
acceptance: A possible match never auto-clears or auto-blocks sign-in; money_held is true while it is open (tested).
Only `clear` against the active baseline versions or a decided not-same-person sets money_held false; `insufficient_name` and `not_screened` keep it true (tested).

The subject, a member of the subject company or a conflicted reviewer cannot decide; not-same-person without a second person fails; two concurrent approvals produce one decision (tested on PostgreSQL under the runtime role).
A decided entry is not flagged again for the same subject unless its normalized names change (tested).
No screening field appears in any public, counterparty, search, federation or agent projection (projection tests).

packages.title: Screening gates for money, commercial commitments, counterparties and agents
packages.goal: No money moves and no commitment binds for a subject who is held, matched, unscreened or screened against stale lists; the gate fails closed (ADR 014 decision 13; Contribuda parity for payouts).
steps: Gate port in apps/api/src/modules/screening-gates: `requireTransactable(subjects, purpose)` reading screening state and holds, refusing with `screening.review_pending`, `screening.unavailable` or `jurisdiction.restricted`, failing closed when the state cannot be read.
Wire the gate into quote sending, order acceptance and agreement binding for both parties (sales, procurement, transactions modules) and into agent commits through the mandate evaluation path.
Payee and payout-country helpers for PAY-001 and BILL-002: a restricted payout country is refused before any provider is called and holds the declaring person (`payout_country`).
Counterparty words: the other side learns only that the party cannot transact now; the subject sees the status words of SANC-003.
Negative and concurrency tests: a decision racing a commitment never lets the commitment bind on a stale answer.
acceptance: A quote, order or agreement involving a held, matched, unscreened or stale-screened party is refused (tested for each party side).
When the screening store is unavailable the gate refuses (tested).
A restricted payout country is refused before the provider fake is called (tested).
Counterparty responses contain no screening detail (projection test).

packages.title: Re-screening on every list update and on schedule
packages.goal: Every active person and company is screened again against each newly activated list version, with a weekly safety net, idempotently and with progress the console can show (ADR 014 decision 12).
steps: On `screening.list_version_activated` enqueue a delta run: subjects whose names could meet changed or added entries first, then all active subjects; batch through the job runner with backpressure.
Weekly scheduled full run (the `sanctions_rescreen` schedule kind of the console contract) and a manual trigger for compliance staff.
Persistence in packages/data/migrations/rescreen: screening_rescreen_run with counts and state; idempotency per (subject, list version); resumable after failure.
Metrics: run duration, subjects per minute, matches opened; an alert when a run fails or exceeds its window.
acceptance: A new list version that adds an entry matching an existing subject opens a review case for that subject without any other trigger (tested).
Running the same delta twice opens no duplicate matches (tested).
A run interrupted half-way resumes without re-screening finished subjects (tested).

packages.title: Console: screening section, holds and matches queue, compliance panel on people and companies
packages.goal: Give compliance staff the screens to run the engine: Trust then Screening (lists and freshness, geolocation table, matches queue, holds, re-screen runs, metrics) and a compliance panel on person and company pages with decisions under a second person (ADR 014 decisions 14 and 18).
steps: HC-74 Screening on the API: baseline lists shown always on, additional lists, freshness, geolocation dataset and age, re-screen runs, cohort metrics.

Matches queue: one item per subject with lateness; the case view shows list entry and screened names side by side; confirm, propose not-same-person (second person through the approvals inbox), appeals to a different reviewer.
Holds: open holds with place, source, dataset and time; clear with reason and evidence category; history.
Compliance panel on person and company pages; notifications that name nobody; the screening namespace in every engine language; keyboard and screen-reader checks.
acceptance: No control can disable a baseline list, loosen matching below the engine rule or clear without a reason (scan and test).
A not-same-person decision cannot complete without a second person against the API (end-to-end test).
The subject's own account never sees the console paths (negative test).

Screening status and holds on the participant card are visible only to roles holding the screening permission; other staff see neither the status nor its absence, except the restricted-servicing notice the hub's legal settings allow (negative test).

packages.title: Refusal and notice copy in every language, legal sections and the participant's compliance page
packages.goal: Say every refusal and notice kindly, truthfully and only as far as the law allows, in every engine language, and let a participant see their own status and appeal (ADR 014 decision 15).
steps: Spanish (and every later engine language) for the jurisdiction namespace; native-speaker review flags for every language.
Mail templates for a hold, a cleared hold, a review pending, a decision and an appeal outcome through the outbox (no list or entry named).
Privacy-notice section "Location and sanctions compliance" and updates to the terms template section, as drafts for counsel; geolocation dataset attribution text.
Settings, Account, Compliance: own status words and the appeal form (`core.compliance_status`, `core.appeal_compliance_decision`), keyboard and screen-reader accessible.
acceptance: Every key of the jurisdiction and screening namespaces exists in every engine language (test).
No notice names a list, an entry or another person (test over templates).
The appeal needs a fresh step-up and reaches a reviewer other than the original decider (tested).

packages.title: Our own services refuse restricted places: federation admission, update channel, registry, hub directory and support
packages.goal: Enforce on what we control instead of a kill switch in the engine (owner decision 2026-10-31, ADR 014 decision 4): a shared admission check from declared jurisdiction, deployment attestation and geolocation on our side, used by federation and by the services Contribuda operates.

Runbook docs/operations/sanctions-our-services.md for the update and release channel, container registry pulls, the public hub directory, support channels and hosted services: which control applies where, who reviews refusals.
Tests with fake manifests, attestations and documentation addresses; FED-001 calls the check at handshake.

The engine gains no code that geolocates its own server or disables itself by location (review checklist item).

packages.title: Deployment-location attestation in the setup wizard
packages.goal: Record where the operator's legal entity and the hosting are, refuse restricted places, audit it and require renewal on change and yearly, complementing the configuration, pack and kernel refusals (owner decision 2026-10-31, ADR 014 decision 4).

packages.title: Counterparty verification adapters and recipes (sanctions screening through the SANC engine)
packages.goal: Turn local registers into evidence: check adapters in fake, manual and live modes, recipes per subject and trigger, results with retention and appeals; the sanctions check calls the screening engine of ADR 014 (SANC-003) instead of keeping its own lists.

Implement adapters with deterministic fakes and a manual-review mode; live mode behind second-person activation and KEYS-001 secret references.

Implement recipes, result evidence records, expiry and re-check scheduling (packages/data/migrations/verification); the `sanctions_screening` check reads and triggers SANC-003 screening and stores only a reference to its result.
Implement review cases and appeals for non-sanctions checks decided by a different reviewer (sanctions matches are reviewed in SANC-003); map results to badge categories and eligibility flags.
Run SANC-003 screening of the claimant and the company before any hand-over level; record the claimed-level domain tie from an outreach invitation link only under the CLM-001 rule.
acceptance: Baseline sanctions screening cannot be disabled; recipes cannot drop the sanctions check (tested).
A potential sanctions match never auto-blocks or auto-clears and blocks the claim until SANC-003 decides it.
Badges show categories, never documents; results expire and trigger re-checks per recipe.
A screening possible match or an unavailable screening store blocks every hand-over level (test).

packages.title: Company identifiers, registrations, licences, claims and per-hub verification badges
packages.goal: Model sourced, claimed and verified honestly: country-pack identifier kinds, state-level registrations and contractor licences, claims through hub recipes and per-hub badges.
steps: Add company_profile, company_identifier (expand from legal_identifiers, then contract), company_registration, tax_registration, company_branch, company_claim and company_verification (packages/data/migrations/claims); contractor licences are professional_credential rows of REP-001 checked through HUB-003.
Derive the company claim status from the strongest active verification in the same transaction.
Implement claim submission and reviewer decisions against recipe versions; decider differs from claimant.
Use the US as the worked example (EIN, Secretary of State registrations, state contractor licences) with synthetic fixtures only.

Hand-over levels: claimed gives limited page control (descriptive fields, suggestions, stopping outreach); verified gives the company administrator role (discovery-and-outreach section 7; owner question 4 may change the split); record handover_record rows.

Disputes and takeover protection: one open claim per page; a second claim opens a claim_dispute decided with a second person; a claim against a claimed or verified page needs verified-level evidence, notifies current administrators and waits a hub-set period (default 7 days); a cooling period (default 7 days) after hand-over blocks changes to legal name, identifiers, website domain, payout details and the representative.
Accept outreach invitation links only as the claimed-level domain tie when the address is on the domain recorded for the company and not a free mail service.
acceptance: An identifier value never upgrades a badge by itself (tested).
Badges show categories and dates, never documents.
Verification expires and re-checks per recipe; revocation updates every projection.
No real company data in fixtures.
No reply, message text or invitation link alone changes a claim status or grants a role (negative test).
Two concurrent claims on one page produce one dispute and no hand-over (concurrency test on PostgreSQL).
Sensitive changes during the cooling period are refused (clock test).

packages.title: Support workspace and account servicing without impersonation

steps: Implement the account summary allowlist projection.
Implement servicing actions with evidence, second person and a 72-hour cooling-off where required (second-factor reset, recovery rebind).
Implement the access explainer returning reason codes only.
Implement user-initiated diagnostic snapshots attached to cases.

Explainer responses contain no private values.

packages.goal: Answer access, deletion, correction and opt-out requests within country-pack deadlines, propagate erasure everywhere and keep lawful evidence.
steps: Add privacy_request, privacy_preference, privacy_export, erasure_ledger (outside the restorable snapshot), legal_hold and data_broker_registration (packages/data/migrations/privacy).
Compose exports from module exporters through projection serializers.
Execute erasure with two people: delete, redact or pseudonymize per module; emit retrieval and federation tombstones as outbox events; replay the ledger after restore.
Honour opt-out of sale or sharing, limits on sensitive data and Global Privacy Control signals as data (US worked example).
Offer a full export of everything a person or company owns in open formats at any time, including after a paid plan ends.

Accept objections, corrections and erasure requests from non-participants who appear in sourced records (form on the page, letter, e-mail) with the minimum tie needed; objections to direct marketing apply immediately and unconditionally.
Keep the minimal suppression entry through erasure and name it in the erasure ledger; add a do-not-collect entry so refreshes do not re-import erased data.
Regulator registry intake as data with a fake adapter (California DROP as the US example: poll interval and deadlines from the pack).

A restore drill with erased-subject fixtures serves nothing erased.

Export remains available after a plan ends and contains only the requester's own data and shared records they may read.
After erasure the person receives no outreach and the next refresh does not re-import their data (test).
An objection submitted while an outreach batch is queued cancels the queued touches (concurrency test).
Privacy request response packages can be prepared by an operator agent at Draft; execution and every decision stay with people (negative test).

packages.title: Hub source registry with licence flags, legal basis and import review
packages.goal: Let a hub register information sources with separate licence flags (display, store, index, model egress, syndicate) and a recorded legal basis; imported items are drafts in a review queue and never publish on their own.
steps: Add source, crawl_policy, import_batch, source_item, sourced_record_field and record_link_proposal (packages/data/migrations/sources).
Record licence flags, robots and terms digests and the legal basis per source; read RSL 1.0 terms as suggestions an editor confirms, never applying a more permissive reading.
Implement takedown: deactivate records, emit retrieval and federation tombstones, audit the reason.
Sponsored content is a per-hub option, off by default, always labelled, never used for ranking, matching or recommendations (ADR 012).
acceptance: No imported item is published without a person's decision (tested).
A display-only source never reaches a model provider or a peer (negative tests).
RSL parsing failures fall back to the most restrictive flags.

packages.title: Pipeline engine and scheduler

Implement runs with leasing, fencing, quotas, retry policy and the state machine.
Implement dry runs with no committed effects.
Implement alerts and automatic pause on source, robots or terms changes.
Support role-bound stages for the editorial agent team: each stage names its role, and per-role caps are checked before every paid call (editorial office section 8.3).
Extend dry runs with an editorial preview: collection decisions per host, items and drafts that would be created, and publications a standing policy would have made, without committing any of them.
Outreach steps (send, notify) are external effects: a run never retries a touch whose outcome is unknown; kill switches cancel queued touches.
acceptance: A dry run commits nothing (tested).
Retries never repeat an external effect with an unknown outcome.

packages.title: Local data mining: datasets and entity resolution
packages.goal: Configurable datasets with legal basis, licence, retention and purpose; refresh pipelines; link proposals, never merges; outputs to directory, verification evidence, eligibility, opportunities, events and knowledge.

Allow a reviewed batch decision for link proposals whose evidence includes an identifier match from a statutory register: one recorded decision by a person who saw a sample and the counts; record the scoring method version with every proposal; support mark-distinct pairs.
acceptance: Court and debt records about natural persons are never displayed (tested).
No dataset output reaches reputation.
People are linked only with their own confirmation; personal-data datasets cannot activate without a recorded legal basis.

A record on the do-not-collect list is dropped before storage on every refresh (test).
Batch acceptance is refused for any proposal without statutory identifier evidence (test).

packages.title: AI provenance and labelling for text, translations and images
packages.goal: Record and show how AI contributed to every publication, translation and image: reader-visible labels naming the responsible human, C2PA manifests and IPTC digital source types on generated images.

Add label strings in every engine language and render them on publications, translations and images.
Behind an adapter with a fake, attach C2PA manifests with IPTC digitalSourceType to generated or AI-edited images.

Generated images carry trainedAlgorithmicMedia or compositeWithTrainedAlgorithmicMedia.

packages.title: Autonomous editorial office with story clusters
packages.goal: Discover and propose sources with recorded legal checks, ingest, deduplicate, cluster stories with multi-source attribution, draft, translate, check facts and similarity, label AI images and fill review queues; people approve every publication.

Implement deduplication and story clusters that reference, never copy, source items and list every source with time and link.

Implement drafting, translation, similarity and fact-check steps behind model routes; display-only sources are excluded from drafting; the review workbench API, calendar and magazine assembly proposals.

Record claim records with evidence spans for every automated draft and add the uncited_claim blocker; order intake by an attention score built only from named, explained signals with no commercial signal (editorial office sections 5.7 and 5.8).
Quarantine imported text with instruction-like content before any drafting; run every extraction, summary and translation call tool-less with schema-validated output (section 5.5).
Build query plans from the hub taxonomy, plan-step categories and glossary, never from imported text (section 5.3).
acceptance: No code path publishes without a person's approval (tested).
A source whose robots or terms change is paused automatically.

Frozen v1 fixtures still validate unchanged.

Implement node, hub, hub module, hub connections, company representative, person and connection kill switches through authorization epochs.

Store hub defaults and maximums for participants' agent settings (approval rules, outreach per week, schedules, report cadence, channels) and the job templates each module offers with default triggers and minimum intervals; a default never exceeds its maximum.

Add the agent_capability kill-switch scope as an additive extension of KillSwitchScopeSchema (shared contract, integrator agreement); compute and store a preview of every policy version (changed modules and capabilities, affected mandates, job subscriptions, connections and runs as cohort counts) so the second person approves what the drafter saw.
acceptance: Turning a job on creates only a mandate proposal; nothing runs until it is confirmed on the first-party form (tested).
Each kill switch blocks the next action check; executing actions go to reconciliation.
No module code path branches on a country code (lint or test).
A capability turned off for a hub, participant type or plan is refused identically through the interface, the agent runtime and MCP (parity test).
No hub configuration key exists that disables mandates, the person's confirmation for commitments, sanctions gates, restricted places or payment neutrality (schema test).
No staff endpoint reads or changes one participant's agent, mandates, settings, goals, job subscriptions or connections (negative authorization tests).
The preview stored with a policy version is the one its approver saw; activation with a stale preview fails.

packages.title: Agent metering, quotas, agent plans and usage statistics
packages.goal: Meter agent usage idempotently, enforce quotas and protection limits, let a hub price modules with versioned, second-person-activated records and see cohort statistics.
steps: Append usage records idempotently per run step, attempt and meter.
Check quota windows per principal, module and meter; reserve estimates from the named platform budget beyond the included quota and settle on actuals.
Implement agent plan versions and metered price versions (cost beside sale price) on offers, price versions and acceptances; protection limits stay independent of plans.

Let plan versions decide module and capability availability (the entitlement port used by AGT-003) and quotas per module and meter; consume prepaid credits under the validity and refund rules of BILL-004 (ADR 012 decision 33).

The preview matches what the runtime then does in a deterministic test.
Every setting has an explanation string in every engine language.
A setting above the hub maximum is refused with an explanation and a tighter setting is always accepted; a change of hub defaults never widens an existing mandate (tests).
No staff principal can read or change a participant's agent settings (negative authorization test).

packages.title: Governed extension registry for agent capabilities
packages.goal: Let hub administrators add functions, tools, integrations and capabilities to agents through a governed registry (ADR 010 decision 22) without ever bypassing mandates, budgets, kill switches, privacy rules, the restricted-places list or the untrusted-text rule.

Each extension names its extension-scoped model route (KEYS-001) and, when it charges, its metered price version (AGT-004); its manifest schema has no key that disables mandates, the person's confirmation, sanctions gates, restricted places or payment neutrality (ADR 010 decision 25).
acceptance: An extension that declares an action without a mandate kind is rejected (tested).

packages.title: Model gateway with egress-policy routing and per-mandate cost caps

Honour provider, model, job, module, capability and extension kill switches at call time; record per-call metadata (route, model version, rollout stage, latency, tokens, cost, fallback used, outcome) without bodies, and aggregate it by model version and by cohort (participant type, plan, module) with counts under ten suppressed.

Concurrent calls cannot exceed a mandate's cost cap.
Logs contain no prompt or response bodies by default.
A fallback or canary version is used only when the egress decision allows it for the call's data class (negative test).
Every call uses exactly the pinned revision of its resolved route; usage aggregates contain no per-person rows.

packages.title: Model catalogue per hub: pinned versions, evaluation before activation, canary rollout, rollback and per-model kill switch
packages.goal: Give the hub administrator complete control over which models serve the hub and how a new model version reaches service (ADR 010 decision 25): a governed catalogue, pinned revisions with one-action rollback, a safety suite and a quality check on hub samples before activation, canary and staged rollout with automatic stop, a per-model kill switch and cost and latency aggregates by cohort.
steps: Contracts in packages/contracts/src/model-catalog.ts: ModelCatalogEntrySchema (connection, provider model id, description per hub language, capabilities, context window, output and file-size limits, processing regions with their source, retention and training terms, status draft, evaluated, enabled, disabled, retired), ModelVersionPinSchema, ModelEvaluationRunSchema and ModelRolloutSchema; propose the additive model kill-switch scope to the integrator.

Catalogue lifecycle with an audit record per change: enabling a model that may receive non-public data needs a second person; retire is terminal; processing regions in restricted places are refused; provider end-of-life dates raise alerts and never substitute a model automatically.

Route validation: every model in an active route is an enabled catalogue entry with a pinned revision and limits within its context window; rollback reactivates the previous pin for the next call while in-flight calls finish on their version.

Evaluation before activation: run the EVAL-001 safety suite against the candidate on its route and data classes through the fake adapter, plus a quality check on hub-defined sample sets (public or synthetic data only) with thresholds compared with the version in service; results expire on an engine update or a provider revision change, and a version that fails after an engine release is suspended.

Staged rollout through the LLM-001 route-resolution port: assignment by a deterministic hash of the run or request id, administrator-chosen stages, guard thresholds that stop the rollout and return all calls to the current version; embeddings never canary; reaching 100 percent on a route carrying non-public data needs a second person.

Aggregates per model version and stage (latency median and 95th percentile, error, fallback, cost and safety-signal rates) and by cohort (participant type, plan, module) with counts under ten suppressed; a preview of every catalogue, pin or rollout change (affected routes and modules, estimated monthly cost).
Support per-role sample sets for editorial agent roles; a model version serves an editorial role only after passing that role's sample set and the safety suite.
acceptance: A route naming a model that is not an enabled catalogue entry, without a pinned revision or with limits above the model's context window cannot be activated (tested).
A model version without a passing safety suite and quality check serves no call (negative test).
Rollback restores the previous pin for the next call; in-flight calls finish on the version they started with (test with a fake clock).
A canary never carries a data class the current version may not carry, and crossing a guard threshold returns all calls to the current version (tests).
Sample sets reject records of a non-public data class; enabling a model for non-public data by its drafter alone fails.
Aggregates never contain a per-person row; the suite runs in npm run check without network access.

An outreach message on SMS or a messenger without recorded prior consent is refused before the adapter is called (test).

packages.title: Counterparty due-diligence pack as a cited platform deliverable
packages.goal: Generate a dated, cited report on one counterparty from sourced facts, verification results the requester may see, sanctions screening outcome, public procurement history and published reputation, billed from the platform budget.
steps: Define the report contract with a citation for every statement and the projection used.
Compose the report through the requester's projection serializer; never read private data of the subject.
Reserve and settle cost under generate_deliverable with the platform budget; show the subject aggregate counts of packs, never who requested them.
Allow a supplier to generate a pack on a buyer or a prospective teaming partner from a pursuit, through the requester projection only.
acceptance: Every statement has a source citation (test).
A requester without rights to a verification result never sees it (negative test).
No pack contains party_private or owner_private fields of the subject.
A pack generated from a pursuit never reveals the pursuit or the requester to the subject (negative test).

packages.title: Events backend: hosting, registration, tickets, check-in and partner meetings
packages.goal: Turn events into a real module: organizers host events under the hub policy, attendees register, buy tickets through the hub's payment provider, check in and meet partners.
steps: Add event, co-organizer, session, speaker consent, ticket type, ticket price version, registration question, registration, ticket, check-in, waitlist, meeting profile, slot, request, material and feedback (packages/data/migrations/events).
Implement organizer use cases with the hub hosting policy and review states.
Implement registration and ticket issuance with quota and capacity under concurrency; paid tickets go through PAY-001.
Implement the offline-first check-in API with duplicate scan detection and opt-in meeting profiles with private declines.
Add hosted-buyer meetings curated by organizers with mutual acceptance and a slot optimiser for personal schedules.
acceptance: Online links and attendee lists never appear in the public projection.
Quotas and capacity hold under concurrent registrations (tested).
A sold ticket keeps its price version; unknown payment outcomes reconcile, never double-charge.
Speakers are shown only with recorded consent; sponsorship and payments never change listing order.
A hosted-buyer meeting needs both sides' acceptance; the optimiser never double-books a person (test).
Organizers taking payments pass the screening gate before ticketing opens (tested).

packages.title: Events on the web: listings, registration, tickets and organizer screens on the API
packages.goal: Wire the existing event pages to the API and add organizer screens.
steps: Wire list, event page, registration, ticket and calendar file to the API through the DataPort.
Build organizer screens (programme, ticket types, registrations, check-in report) with every state.
Strings in an events locale namespace; Playwright and axe at three widths.
acceptance: Registration and ticket purchase work against the API with the fake payment provider.
Keyboard, screen reader and narrow-screen checks pass.

packages.title: Courses, assessments and verifiable certificates
packages.goal: Courses with versions, assessments and certificates that anyone can check by number, shown on the personal profile.
steps: Model course, version, lesson, assessment, attempt, certificate and accreditation record (packages/data/migrations/learning).
Implement authoring with the hub editorial review policy; certificate issuance, public check projection and revocation with reason.
Keep learning progress private to the learner; no employer view.
Connect the «Моя страница» learning tab and /certificates/:id to the API.
acceptance: A certificate names the course version and never changes; revocation is a status with reason.
No certificate shows an accreditation without a recorded source.
Progress is never exposed to employers or other members.

packages.title: Capability profiles, needs board, explainable matching and introductions
packages.goal: Help clients, contractors, suppliers and partners find each other with explainable, payment-blind matching and double-opt-in introductions.
steps: Model capability profiles with per-field visibility, open needs, partner posts, match method versions, runs, candidates, introductions, outreach quotas and alert subscriptions (packages/data/migrations/matching).
Implement hard eligibility (region, licence, sanctions) with pass, fail and unknown results.
Implement versioned ranking with explanations and uncertainty over structured attributes (semantic recall arrives with RAG-301); requester-tunable weights.
Implement introductions with quotas shared by people and their agents, labelled agent requests, contact reveal on acceptance and alerts.
Sourced external candidates can be contacted only through the outreach gate chain of OUTR-002 under the hub policy; in strict mode the interface keeps the outreach-not-permitted note.
Accept partner requests from pursuits (BID-006): candidates for a scope, explained and payment-blind, through double-opt-in introductions within the shared quota.
acceptance: Rankings are identical with and without paid entitlements (test).
Matching never reads private quotes, budgets or floors.
Contact details appear only after an introduction is accepted; unknown eligibility is shown as unknown.
In a hub whose outreach policy is strict, no matching or introduction path sends anything to a sourced company (test).
Partner candidates never reveal whether a candidate follows or bids for the same opportunity (negative test).

packages.title: Lead honesty: consented fan-out for private-client needs and no per-lead charging
packages.goal: Guarantee that a private client's need reaches only providers the client chose or consented to, under a hub-configured cap, and that no price version can charge per lead, introduction or received RFQ.
steps: Add a fan-out cap and an explicit consent record to private-client needs.
Reject offer and price-version definitions whose billable unit is a lead, introduction or received RFQ.
Record need outcomes so the board stays honest; show the client how many providers saw the need.

Publish the lead-honesty charter (no per-lead fees, fan-out cap, no resale) as a versioned hub setting and add a request receipt: the client sees who received the request and why; each recipient sees it was not sold and how many others received it.
acceptance: A need is never delivered to more providers than the client consented to (concurrency test).
The billing schema rejects per-lead units.
Providers never see other providers' responses.
A request receipt lists exactly the recipients and never more (test).

packages.title: Needs board, partner posts and introductions on the web
packages.goal: Give participants the matching screens: needs board, partner posts, explained candidates with uncertainty, introduction requests and responses.
steps: Screen contracts and screens for needs, partner posts, candidates with explanations and introductions.
Strings in a matching locale namespace; Playwright and axe at three widths.
From an open need or an imported public opportunity, offer "Follow in Tenders" that creates a pursuit in the bid desk.
acceptance: Every candidate shows why it matched and what is unknown.
Contact details appear only after acceptance (browser test with two personas).
The needs board never shows how many companies follow an opportunity (browser test).

packages.title: Public opportunities and awards: open needs, bid calendar and sourced track record
packages.goal: Import public opportunities (SAM.gov for the US hub, state and municipal portals where terms permit, OCDS elsewhere) as read-only open needs, show a bid calendar and record awards as sourced project history.
steps: Map SAM.gov notices, USAspending awards and OCDS releases to open-need and sourced-project contracts.
Implement importers with fakes as pipelines; record each portal's reuse terms; keys only as KEYS-001 secret references.
Link awards to companies only through identifiers, never by name alone; add a bid calendar for followed needs.

Expose followed notices to the supplier bid desk as pursuit sources (BID-001) with structured deadlines in the buyer time zone, the official clarification channel and amendment links taken from structured notice data only.
acceptance: Imported needs cannot receive Trustwork RFQ responses unless their owner is a participant who published them.
Awards linked by name only are rejected.
Statistics use only public award data.
Notices whose buyer, place of performance or delivery is in a restricted place are never stored or shown (test).
Deadlines and clarification channels come only from structured fields, never from document text (test).

packages.title: Privacy-safe benchmarking for companies
packages.goal: Show a company its own response time, win rate and on-time delivery next to anonymised peer aggregates, only above a minimum group size and never at employee level.
steps: Define company-level metrics from structured records the company participates in.
Compute peer aggregates by category and region with a minimum group size and noise where needed.
Show method, period and group size beside every comparison.
acceptance: No aggregate is shown below the minimum group size (test).
No metric is computed per employee; private prices never enter any aggregate.

packages.title: Homeowner journey and home passport
packages.goal: Give private clients a guided path from photos and a goal to a plan, consented matching and staged payments, and at completion a home passport with maintenance reminders, structured warranty claims and transfer on sale.
steps: Define home passport, installed item, warranty and warranty-claim contracts owned by the homeowner.
Fill the passport from accepted deliveries and field records; remind before maintenance and warranty deadlines.
Transfer the passport to a new owner only with the current owner's consent; contractors keep their own evidence copies.
Offer milestone payment templates with deposit limits and cancellation rights from the country or state pack for private clients.
acceptance: Home passports are owner_private and never federate (negative tests).
Warranty claims reach only the contractor named on the installed item.
Estimates always show their sources and the word estimate.
A consumer template cannot exceed the pack's deposit limit (test).

packages.title: Permission-separated ingestion and index lifecycle
packages.goal: Build reproducible derived projections and pgvector generations under the accepted schema, fed by the outbox.
steps: Add the retrieval tables in packages/data/migrations/retrieval (pgvector introduced here with a written dependency reason); the module owns only its own directory, schema mirror and repository file.

Implement outbox-fed projection, extraction and embedding with fakes, then only separately authorized adapters reusing the accepted BE-001 admission and revocation primitive; never duplicate the gate.
Test quarantine, duplicate events, taint, backfill, deletion and rollback; record the exact build.
acceptance: No mixed-audience embedding; current purpose and egress rights are checked before extraction and dispatch.
Idempotence, out-of-order changes, locator quarantine, deletion, revocation and restore tombstone replay demonstrated.
Generation activation and rollback are fenced by current policy and source watermark.
A revoke between preflight and dispatch prevents new admission (integration test).

packages.title: Governed hybrid retrieval and delivery fencing
packages.goal: Deliver structured and semantic plans with current field and party rights and grounded citations.
steps: Implement typed runtime queries, the structured resolver and hybrid fusion inside the trusted boundary.
Reuse the BE-001 admission and revocation primitive for query embedding, reranking, answer dispatch and final response and citation delivery.
Exercise public-private taint, provider injection, no-answer, freshness and budget exhaustion.
acceptance: Private authorized exact subsets and public-only certified ANN; measured plans and filtered recall.
Candidates, hydration, provider egress and final admission fail closed on revoke; multi-node race tested.
Saved answers inherit the intersection of source rights; exact identifiers and complete-domain calculations bypass top-k.
Federated replicas are indexed only under their own source class and licence; no private query or private context is ever forwarded to a peer (tested).

packages.title: Search, cited answers and freshness states on the web
packages.goal: Expose understandable multilingual search and citation experiences using the frozen contracts.
steps: Integrate search and the source drawer in the search page and dialog.
Test keyboard and mobile states, revoked citations and stale RFQ comparisons.
Strings in a search locale namespace for every engine language.
acceptance: Search and citations honour current access without hidden counts or unauthorized previews.
Partial, no-answer, unavailable, historical and stale states are readable and accessible.
Citations open exact permitted versions.

packages.title: Verify real RAG quality, security, scale and recovery
packages.goal: Produce actual model, database, adversarial and restore evidence before standalone release QA.
steps: Run the evaluation protocol with a pinned authorized model, database and hardware.
Exercise the adversarial boundary matrix and three 30-minute load runs per selected tier.
Record limitations, regressions, provider and cost policy and rollback drills for independent review.
acceptance: A frozen held-out multilingual and no-answer corpus with quality and citation metrics per stratum.
Zero authorization leakage across candidate, context, provider, delivery, citation, cache and history with revocation races.
No acceptance inferred from fake fixtures; unresolved target failures block QA.

packages.title: Cacheable, indexable and lighter public pages
packages.goal: Serve published content from caches with per-language URLs and route-level CSS: English without a prefix, other languages with a language prefix and hreflang alternates, no country in public URLs (ADR 012 decision 27).
steps: Implement ADR 012 decision 27: English unprefixed, other languages under /<lang>/ with hreflang alternates and canonical URLs; the language cookie redirects only from unprefixed entry pages; no country segment.
Remove the global force-dynamic; render published content statically or with revalidation; keep personalized parts dynamic.
Split the public stylesheet into route-level CSS modules.
Add Web Vitals budgets for the main public templates on a mobile profile.
acceptance: Anonymous news, article, magazine and directory pages are served from cache with correct language variants.
Mobile performance budgets pass in CI for the home, news and company templates.
No private or personalized data is ever cached for another visitor (tested).

packages.title: Specify the mesh protocol and federation contracts
packages.goal: Freeze the federation protocol of ADR 011 as contracts and conformance vectors before any implementation.
steps: Define manifest, global identifier, envelope, feed page, inbox delivery, tombstone, peering record and link proposal schemas.
Specify the signature base and key rotation; publish test vectors.
Specify which projections each object kind may carry and enforce it in the schema.
Write the protocol specification document for implementers outside this repository.
acceptance: Envelopes with party_private or owner_private projections are rejected by schema.
Signature and digest vectors verify in tests.
Restricted jurisdictions are rejected at manifest validation.

packages.title: Node identity, manifest, signatures and peering records
packages.goal: Each node gets a signing key, a signed manifest, key rotation and peering agreements with levels.
steps: Generate and store the node key through the secret store; serve the signed manifest at /.well-known/trustwork/manifest.json.
Implement request signing and verification (packages/data/migrations/federation-node).
Implement peering agreements with levels and second-person approval for deal-routing and identity.
Implement defederation.
acceptance: Unsigned or wrongly signed requests are rejected.
Peering above syndicate needs a second approver.
Defederation stops feeds and deliveries without rewriting history.
A peer whose manifest, attestation or observed server location is a restricted place is refused at handshake through the SANC-008 admission check (tested).

Admission is re-run whenever a peer's manifest, attestation or capability statement changes and before the first delivery of every new deal; a lapsed admission stops new deliveries without rewriting history (tested).

Peers' manifests are refreshed at least daily and immediately after federation.key_unknown; a published revocation triggers re-verification of replicas and deal objects signed at or after compromisedSince (tested).

Acceptance of a peering request is a handshake from the accepting node; a record becomes active on a side only after admission and a person's acceptance (double opt-in), with a second approver for deal_routing and identity (tested).
A changed peer manifest or attestation re-runs the SANC-008 admission; an expired attestation or a refused re-admission suspends all flows with that peer (tested).
Peering records and admission refusal records hold no network address (tested).

packages.title: Public syndication, replicas and tombstones
packages.goal: Public publications, issues, events and directory records flow between peered nodes as signed replicas with provenance, licences and tombstones.
steps: Implement cursor feeds per stream on the home node.
Implement pulling, verification and storage of read-only replicas (packages/data/migrations/federation-syndication).
Respect syndication flags from source licences and author licences of knowledge items.
Apply tombstones within the agreed period and purge indexes and caches.
acceptance: Replicas are read-only and never satisfy a write authorization.
Items with syndication none never leave their node.
Tombstones reach search indexes and caches.
A linked edition travels with its own licence and machine-translation label, never looser than its original, and is never presented as the original (tested).
A replica is never re-served in a feed; editions of a corrected original are marked stale on the receiving node (tested).
Feeds and pulls consult a per-peer stream policy port (default: everything the level and agreed licences allow) so NET-002 can narrow them without changing syndication code.

A purge-by-peer operation removes a peer's replicas from replicas, search indexes, caches and saved answers, personal-data classes (person profiles, reputation snapshots, passport credentials) first (tested).

packages.title: Directory federation and entity links
packages.goal: Companies and people known to several nodes are linked, never merged, with canonical display by claim strength and attributed verification badges.
steps: Implement link proposals from identifier matches and signed statements (packages/data/migrations/federation-links).
Implement data steward review on both nodes.
Display canonical records with field provenance; show peer verification badges only at trust-verifications level, labelled.
acceptance: No automatic merge.
A peer badge is always labelled with the granting node.
Reputation is never recomputed on a replica.
Identifiers from different country packs never create a link by themselves; a company linked across countries keeps each country's identifiers separately (tested).
Links to records on a suspended peer are hidden; on defederation they are marked ended and kept as history, never merged (tested).

packages.title: Cross-node deals and agent envelopes
packages.goal: Participants on different nodes exchange introductions, RFQ invitations, quote versions and agreements with identical digests on both sides.
steps: Deliver shared_party envelopes to the counterparty's home node only.
Verify digests on both sides; bind acceptance to the same agreement digest.
Keep mandates, budgets and approvals on each party's own node; deliver agent envelopes with labels and rate limits per peering.

Before the first commercial message of a context, run the SANC-004 gate on the counterparty and the own participant on each node and exchange outcome-only screening attestations once trustwork-mesh/2 is available (until then each node relies on its own gate).
Pin the exchange schema versions of a deal at its first cross-hub version and use them for every later object of the context.
acceptance: Both nodes hold identical accepted terms proven by the same digest.
Nothing on one node can authorize an action on the other.
No delivery is routed through a third node.

No commercial message leaves or is accepted unless the sending and the receiving node each have a clear screening outcome on fresh lists for both parties; a refusal reveals no match or list (tested on both sides).
Participants' places, the delivery place and any declared origin in a restricted place refuse the deal before any delivery (tested).
Budgets, floors, evaluation weights, mandate contents and cross-border private notes never appear in any envelope (forbidden-field test over every deal kind).
A seller's quote, price or participation is never relayed to another seller on any node (tested).
Unknown delivery outcomes are reconciled by resending the identical body under the same delivery identifier, never by a new identifier (fault-injection test).
Cross-hub request kinds and cross-border deals are refused when the per-peer interaction settings (NET-002) turn them off or exceed their per-hour limits (tested).

packages.title: Federated sign-in between peered nodes
packages.goal: A person can register for an event or answer an RFQ on a peered node without a second account, at identity peering level.
steps: Implement nodes as OIDC providers and relying parties for each other (packages/data/migrations/federation-identity).
Represent remote identities as (node, subject) pairs; never link by e-mail.
Limit what a remote identity may do to what the peering level allows.
acceptance: No auto-linking by e-mail.
A remote identity never gains local company authority.
Ending peering at identity level ends remote sessions.
A remote identity can never accept an agreement or place an order for a company on the receiving node (negative test).
The person's role as consumer or business is carried with the assertion and shown to the counterparty.
Sign-in assertions are accepted only while the per-peer policy port allows identity for that peer (tested).

packages.title: Outbound ActivityPub bridge for publications, issues and public events
packages.goal: Let the wider social web follow a hub: one outbound ActivityPub actor per hub publishing public publications, magazine issues and public events with attribution, corrections as updates and deletions as tombstones.
steps: Map public publication versions, issues and events to ActivityPub objects with links back to the hub.
Honour source licences: items marked syndication none never leave the node.
Accept follows; do not import replies or mentions in the first version; send Update on correction and Delete on retraction or erasure.
acceptance: Only public-projection fields appear in outgoing objects (negative tests).
Restricted-place instances are refused.
No inbound social content is stored except follow records.
Outgoing objects carry language tags (contentMap) and the machine-translation label; an edition is never published as an original (tested).

packages.title: Portable reputation passport: hub-issued verifiable credentials
packages.goal: Let participants export holder-controlled, verifiable credentials of identity checks, licences, certificates, contributions and reputation snapshots, issued by their home hub as W3C Verifiable Credentials 2.0 compatible with Open Badges 3.0 and signed with node keys (ADR 012).
steps: Pin the VC 2.0 and Open Badges 3.0 versions and the issuer identifier on the hub domain; define credential types per hub bound to verification recipes.
Issue credentials signed with the node key through an adapter with a fake; course certificates of LRN-001 as Open Badges.
Publish status lists for revocation and expiry; short validity for snapshot credentials.
Let peers at trust-verifications level show credentials as verified by hub X; record external issuer confirmations as "confirmed by issuer on date", never as issued by Trustwork.
acceptance: Credentials verify offline against the node's published key.
Revoking a verification or licence check updates the status list before the next verification.
Credentials contain no counterparties' private data and no documents; payment never adds, hides or reorders passport contents (test).
Presentations are holder-bound, name their audience and expire quickly; a verifier on another node can check them with only the issuing node's public key chain and status list (tested).
No credential or presentation contains review text, observations or counterparties' identities (tested).

packages.title: Verify the standalone release candidate
packages.goal: Produce real standalone acceptance evidence across the whole product before any public deployment proposal.
steps: Run exact-head integrated checks and authorization, concurrency and fault suites.
Perform manual accessibility and browser journeys for plan to people, reputation, commerce, console and agents.
Restore synthetic data and objects with erasure replay and providers disabled.
Prove no required external development-platform dependency; document release risks, providers and legal gates.
acceptance: Named, non-empty exact-head CI and an independent review.
Restore, permission and unknown-outcome tests demonstrated, not asserted.
Production provider, jurisdiction, RPO and RTO gates resolved before release authorization.

packages.title: Deferred administration screens (superseded)
packages.goal: Superseded on 2026-10-31 (ADR 012): the sources, calendar, methodology, taxonomy, retrieval operations, providers, health, privacy and consent screens are now console slices HUBC-002 to HUBC-006 with live wiring in HUBC-008 to HUBC-010.
steps: None; see HUBC-002 to HUBC-006.
acceptance: Not applicable: superseded.

packages.title: Right-to-left support: direction per locale, logical CSS, mirrored icons and bidi isolation
packages.goal: Make a right-to-left language a translation, not a redesign: Arabic first (LANG-AR), then any right-to-left language a contributor brings. Comes after WEB-005 so the public stylesheets are converted once, after they are split per route.
steps: Derive the text direction from the locale (Intl.Locale text information where the runtime has it, with a fallback list) in apps/web/app/_lib/direction.ts and set lang and dir on the html element; elements that show user content use dir="auto".

Replace physical CSS properties (left, right, margin-left, padding-right, border-left, text-align: left and similar) with logical ones (inset-inline-start, margin-inline-start, padding-inline-end, text-align: start …) in the owned global, locale, auth and public stylesheets and the design-system styles; add a test that fails on new physical properties in those files.

Mirror directional icons (arrows, chevrons, back and forward, progress) in right-to-left and keep non-directional ones (the three-squares mark, logos, media controls, check marks) unmirrored; mark each icon as mirrorable or not in packages/ui/src/components/Icon.

Isolate mixed-direction text with bdi or unicode-bidi: isolate for names, identifiers, numbers, prices, URLs and code inside right-to-left sentences, and for right-to-left names quoted in left-to-right sentences.
Add browser tests with a test-only pseudo right-to-left locale (mirrored English, never offered to visitors) so the layout can be verified before any Arabic string exists.
acceptance: With a right-to-left locale every public and workspace page renders a mirrored layout with no clipped text, overlapping elements or horizontal scrolling at 320 px and 1280 px (browser tests with screenshots).
Directional icons mirror; the brand mark and media controls do not (tested).
Latin names, numbers, prices and identifiers inside right-to-left text keep their order (bidi isolation tested).
No physical left or right property remains in the owned stylesheets (test), and left-to-right pages are visually unchanged (screenshot comparison).
Keyboard focus order and screen-reader reading order follow the visual order in right-to-left.

packages.title: CJK and Devanagari typography: font fallbacks, line breaking, no forced uppercase
packages.goal: Make Chinese, Japanese and Hindi (and later Korean and other Indic scripts) read naturally, with correct fonts, line breaking and emphasis, without shipping large font files to every visitor. Ordered after INTL-005 because both change the root layout and the global stylesheet.
steps: Extend the font stacks per script with :lang() rules, system fonts first (for example PingFang SC, Microsoft YaHei and Noto Sans SC; Hiragino Sans, Yu Gothic and Noto Sans JP; Noto Sans Devanagari and Nirmala UI); add an OFL web-font subset only where a system font is missing, with its provenance in packages/ui/fonts/PROVENANCE.md; never put a full CJK font in the default bundle.

Line breaking: line-break: strict and normal word breaking for Chinese and Japanese (keep-all only where tested), overflow-wrap: anywhere for long identifiers and URLs, no automatic hyphenation for CJK; line heights that never clip Devanagari conjuncts, vowel signs or combining marks.
Remove forced text-transform: uppercase and wide letter-spacing for scripts without letter case through :lang() overrides or tokens; emphasis uses weight rather than italics for CJK.

Search tokenization note: PostgreSQL full-text search has no Chinese or Japanese segmenter and only a simple configuration for Hindi; confirm and extend the requirements recorded in docs/engine/search-and-knowledge.md (n-gram or a segmenter adapter, Unicode normalization, width folding for Japanese) for WEB-003 and RAG-201; do not change search code in this package.
Add browser tests with pseudo text in Han, Kana and Devanagari at 320 px and 1280 px.
acceptance: Han, Kana and Devanagari text renders in a script-appropriate font, never as missing-glyph boxes (browser screenshots in Chromium plus a recorded manual check on other systems).
Japanese and Chinese lines never start with closing punctuation or a full stop, and words never split mid-character cluster in the tested pages.
No forced uppercase or wide letter-spacing applies to scripts without case (test).
The default page weight does not grow for visitors who do not use these scripts (bundle budget test).

packages.title: Locale review status: per-locale metadata shown in the language picker and the docs
packages.goal: Every locale carries an honest review status (English is the reference; others are machine draft, community reviewed or native reviewed) that readers see in the language picker and contributors see in the docs, so no translation claims a review that did not happen (ADR 012 decision 30).
steps: Define the metadata contract in packages/i18n-runtime/src/review-status.ts: status (reference, machine_draft, community_reviewed, native_reviewed), reviewers by public handle and only with their consent, review date, the namespaces the review covered, and a link to the review issue or pull request.

Add apps/web/locales/<locale>.meta.json beside each locale directory (not inside it, so the namespace parity test does not treat it as a namespace) for the six engine languages with the recorded state: en reference; uz-Latn, ka, hy and az-Latn machine draft (produced by the integrator); ru as the owner records it. A locale without metadata is treated as machine draft.
Show the status in the language picker as a short localized label with an accessible description, and on a public note about translations; never hide a language because it is a draft.

Add scripts/locale-status.mjs, which prints the languages table for docs/engine/localization.md from the metadata, and document how a reviewer moves a locale to community or native reviewed through a pull request.
acceptance: Every enabled locale shows its review status in the picker; an unreviewed locale is labelled machine draft (tested).
A locale without metadata is shown as machine draft, never as reviewed (tested).
Review labels exist in every engine language and are announced by screen readers.
The printed table matches the languages table in the localization chapter at merge time.
Locale review status is available in a machine-readable form that capability statements can publish.

packages.title: Portuguese (pt) with formats per country (pt-BR, pt-PT)
packages.goal: Portuguese across the interface and demo content through configuration only, for hubs in Brazil, Portugal and Portuguese-speaking Africa; formats follow the country (pt-BR in Brazil, pt-PT in Portugal), as decided for Spanish (ADR 012 decision 10).
steps: Add pt files for every namespace in apps/web/locales/pt and the design system dictionary packages/ui/locales/pt.json with full key coverage and CLDR plural forms as Intl.PluralRules reports them; translate from English, the reference.
Write Brazilian construction vocabulary first and record terms that differ in European Portuguese as review notes; propose a pt-PT vocabulary overlay as a separate package only if reviewers need one.
Add pt overrides for the demo content (the synthetic US demo hub of DEMO-US, so the translation covers the content that ships).
Register pt through configuration (no TypeScript change) and extend the locale and leak tests to pt.

Record the review status in apps/web/locales/pt.meta.json (machine draft until reviewers sign off), update the languages table in the localization chapter, and open a review request for Portuguese speakers.
acceptance: No missing or placeholder keys in pt; the brand reads Trustwork.
Every public page renders in pt without Russian or untranslated text (leak test).
With country BR dates, numbers and currency use pt-BR formats; with country PT they use pt-PT.
The language picker and the languages table in the localization chapter show the review status (machine draft, community reviewed or native reviewed); no review is claimed that did not happen.

packages.title: French (fr) with formats per country (fr-FR, fr-CA and others)
packages.goal: French across the interface and demo content through configuration only, for hubs in France, Canada, Belgium, Switzerland and French-speaking Africa; formats follow the country.
steps: Add fr files for every namespace in apps/web/locales/fr and the design system dictionary packages/ui/locales/fr.json with full key coverage and CLDR plural forms as Intl.PluralRules reports them; translate from English, the reference.
Keep French typography in the strings (non-breaking spaces before ; : ! ? and guillemets « » where the country uses them); record Canadian French vocabulary differences as review notes for CTRY-CA.
Add fr overrides for the demo content (the synthetic US demo hub of DEMO-US, so the translation covers the content that ships).
Register fr through configuration (no TypeScript change) and extend the locale and leak tests to fr.

Record the review status in apps/web/locales/fr.meta.json (machine draft until reviewers sign off), update the languages table in the localization chapter, and open a review request for French speakers.
acceptance: No missing or placeholder keys in fr; the brand reads Trustwork.
Every public page renders in fr without Russian or untranslated text (leak test).
With country FR dates and numbers use fr-FR formats; with country CA they use fr-CA.
