packages.title: Approval routes, decisions and delegation
packages.goal: Let each company configure versioned approval routes per subject kind with built-in segregation of duties, bind every approval to the exact subject digest and keep approvals human.
steps: Migrations for approval_route_version, approval_request, approval_decision and approval_delegation in packages/data/migrations/approval-routes.
Resolve route steps from conditions and approver selectors (permission holders in the project or company, named person, project leader, quorum); escalate on timeout, never approve by silence.
Enforce segregation of duties (requester never approves; payee-change verifier never alone approves the first payment) and delegation limits.
Expose route activation and decisions as use cases; decisions require a person on the first-party surface.
acceptance: A new subject version supersedes the pending request (test).
A requester or a delegate above the delegator's rights cannot decide (negative tests).
No mandate, extension or connection can produce an approval decision (test).
Concurrent decisions on the same step resolve once (real PostgreSQL test).

packages.title: Requisitions, allocations, call-offs and imports
packages.goal: Let site staff and departments raise versioned requisitions, approve them through routes, and let buyers allocate and merge lines into needs, RFQs, call-offs, external orders and stock transfers with progress back to the requester.
steps: Migrations for requisition, requisition_version, requisition_line and requisition_allocation; call_off and external_order with the framework terms extension agreed with the integrator.
CSV and XLSX import against a published template creating drafts only, with row-level errors.
Allocation commands with a serialized check that allocations never exceed requested quantities; call-offs never exceed the framework.
External orders reserve the transaction budget like platform orders and are never shown as platform transactions.
acceptance: Concurrent allocations cannot exceed the requested quantity (test on real PostgreSQL).
Changing a submitted requisition creates a new version and supersedes approvals (test).
Requisitions are visible only to the requester, approvers and members with project scope (negative tests).
External orders produce no reputation records (test).

packages.title: Company supplier base and external counterparties
packages.goal: Give each company a private supplier base linked to directory entries without leaking, with external counterparties for suppliers not on the platform, supplier cards from own records and private assessments.
steps: Migrations for supplier_record, external_counterparty and supplier_assessment.
Link records to claimed, verified or sourced companies by reading only their public projection.
Compute supplier cards from the buyer's own agreements, orders, receipts, matches and documents.
Import suppliers from CSV or XLSX as private records only.
acceptance: A supplier never learns it is listed, its status or the notes (forbidden-field tests across projections, search, notifications and federation).
An import never creates a directory member, claim or public record (test).
Assessments never enter reputation snapshots (test).

packages.title: Sourcing events: bid levelling, award decisions and outcome notices
packages.goal: Add buyer-private, versioned bid-levelling sheets over pinned quote versions, award decisions through approval routes, sealed-until-deadline RFQs, prequalification eligibility rules and outcome notices without competitors' prices.
steps: Migrations for bid_level_sheet, bid_level_sheet_version, award_decision and bid_outcome_notice.
Pin quote versions by id and digest; mark stale versions non-comparable; keep buyer adjustments separate and labelled.
Execute approved awards only through COM-002 agreement and order commands with authority and budget reservation.
Read prequalification passport sections shared by consent (PREQ-001) as eligibility evidence where available; unknown stays unknown.
acceptance: A levelling sheet never reaches a seller (forbidden-field tests).
Outcome notices carry no other bidder identity or price; bands appear only after award with the buyer's opt-in (tests).
Supplier invitation order is identical with and without paid entitlements (comparison test).

packages.title: AI document intake with confidence and human review
packages.goal: Turn quotes, invoices, credit notes, delivery notes, price lists and takeoffs into reviewed drafts: structured parsing or model extraction with confidence and locators, line and unit matching, discrepancy and duplicate flags, never auto-approval.
steps: Migrations for intake_document, extraction_run, extraction_review and line_match.
Extraction adapter port with a deterministic fake; structured UBL parsing; model routes only through the gateway and the hub egress matrix.
Normalize units through the unit catalogue and sourced packaging conversions; flag discrepancies against RFQ, quote and order lines.
Human review queue: accepted reviews create drafts only; meter document pages.
Keep the extraction adapter port and review queue reusable for tender documents (BID-002): fields carry a citation with document id, version digest, page and region.
acceptance: No intake path creates an approved, ordered or paid record (test).
Text in a document never changes a payee, sends a message or calls a tool (injection suite).
Every extracted field carries confidence and locator (contract test); egress refused for disallowed data classes (test).
The extraction port returns a locator with page and region for every extracted field of a PDF tender document (contract test).

packages.title: Equivalence rules, approved equals and substitutions
packages.goal: Compare equivalent materials through sourced equivalence rules on plan-step terms and product attributes, and decide substitutions only through people (the designer of record where named).
steps: Migrations for equivalence_rule_version, product_unit_conversion and substitution_request.
Match lines as equivalent only by a rule that cites its basis; keep equivalent distinct from approved.
Route substitution requests through the approval route kind substitution; keep approved equals with scope and expiry.
Expose equivalence results to the supplier's specification checks (BID-004) through a read use case over public and company-private rules.
acceptance: No agent or rule approves a substitution (test).
A rule without a basis citation cannot be activated (test).
Conversions without a source stay unconverted and flagged (test).
A supplier specification check shows equivalent by rule only with the rule and its basis and never marks a substitution approved (test).

packages.title: Project budgets and cost control
packages.goal: Show planned, committed, actual, forecast and paid per cost code under each project transaction budget, warn before overruns and route budget changes through approvals.
steps: Migrations for cost_code, budget_line, budget_change and the append-only cost_entry ledger.
Post commitments from accepted orders, call-offs and external orders, releases at order close, actuals from approved trade invoices, idempotently per source.
Warnings at configurable thresholds as decisions waiting; keep the atomic reservation as the hard stop.
acceptance: Cost entries are idempotent per source and balance against their sources (tests).
Budgets and cost codes never reach suppliers, invited experts or staff without a case grant (negative tests).
A budget increase applies only after approval (test).

packages.title: Goods receipts, dispatch notices, discrepancies and offline capture
packages.goal: Record what arrives at a site or warehouse against orders, partial and offline, with photos, typed discrepancies, supplier notices and returns, separate from quality acceptance.
steps: Migrations for dispatch_notice, goods_receipt, goods_receipt_line and supplier_return.
Offline sync API with client ids, device and server times and idempotent replay.
Order-line balance view (ordered, dispatched, received, accepted, invoiced, returned, open); optional acceptance_record creation for delivery claims.
Discrepancy notices to platform suppliers and drafted messages for external ones.
acceptance: A replayed offline receipt never duplicates (test).
Photo location and faces never appear outside the buyer and that supplier (test).
A receipt never counts as confirmed acceptance unless a person records it (test).

packages.title: Site stock, movements and transfers
packages.goal: Keep stock per site, warehouse, yard and vehicle as an append-only movement ledger with transfers, issues to work, returns, write-offs and reorder suggestions, without per-person tracking.
steps: Migrations for stock_location, stock_item, stock_movement and stock_transfer.
Compute balances per item and location; corrections append.
Reorder points propose requisition drafts only.
acceptance: No query or report aggregates movements per person (test over the analytics views).
Concurrent issues cannot drive a balance negative without an explicit flagged adjustment (test).
Stock locations in a restricted place are refused (test).

packages.title: Trade invoices, three-way match and duplicate detection
packages.goal: Receive invoices between participants or from external suppliers, match them with orders and receipts within tolerances, detect duplicates, route exceptions and approvals, and show suppliers their invoice status.
steps: Migrations for trade_invoice, trade_invoice_version, trade_invoice_line, match_tolerance_policy_version and invoice_match.
Two-, three- and four-way match with company tolerances; recompute on new receipts, credit notes and versions.
Duplicate and risk signals (payment_risk_signal) before approval; approval through the route creates actual cost entries.
Supplier-visible status (received, in review, approved, scheduled, paid, disputed) without internal approvers or notes.
acceptance: A suspected duplicate cannot be approved until a person clears it (test).
Issued invoice versions are immutable; corrections reference the corrected version (trigger test).
Match results and approval records never reach the issuer (forbidden-field tests).

packages.title: Payment proposals, instructions and payee protection
packages.goal: Prepare and approve payment proposals, execute instructions only through the hub's licensed providers or record external payments with evidence, and protect payees against bank-detail and invoice fraud.
steps: Migrations for payment_proposal, payment_proposal_version, payment_instruction, payee_account, payee_change_request and payment_risk_signal.
Payee accounts as provider tokens with masked display and keyed fingerprint; changes only from the holder company account with a second factor, callback to a contact on file and cooling-off.
Instructions through the PAY-001 port with stable idempotency keys; unknown outcomes reconciled; external_recorded mode with evidence.
Business-email-compromise and urgency signals on procurement threads; open signals block approval and release.
acceptance: No table or log stores an account number (schema and log tests).
A payee change from a document, e-mail or agent is refused and raises a signal (test).
Concurrent instructions never exceed an invoice's open amount; a timeout never pays twice (tests on real PostgreSQL with the fake provider).
Configurations routing funds through an operator account are refused (test).

packages.title: Document types, completeness and e-invoicing networks
packages.goal: Use country-pack document types and company requirement sets to check completeness of supplier onboarding, orders, receipts, invoices and handovers, and exchange e-documents through network adapters with fakes.
steps: Migrations for document_requirement_set, document_link and e_document_exchange.
A UBL 2.1 serializer and parser and a fake access point; a network adapter port keyed by pack network codes.
Completeness as a condition usable in approval routes; document approvals through the route kind document.
acceptance: Requirement sets referencing a type the bound pack lacks are rejected (test).
Exchange records are unique per network and external id; unknown outcomes reconcile (test).
No Russian network or provider can be configured (test against the restricted list).

A cross-hub e-document is exchanged over a network both parties' packs list (Peppol preferred where both have participant identifiers); otherwise only a reference with the document digest crosses nodes (tested).

packages.title: Accounting, ERP and project-tool exports and imports
packages.goal: Map suppliers, cost codes, purchase orders, receipts, approved invoices, credit notes and payments to accounting and ERP systems, and import one's own budgets, commitments and vendors from construction project tools, all through adapters with fakes.
steps: Object mappings and idempotent export jobs with digests of what was sent.
Fake adapters first; candidate live adapters for QuickBooks Online, Xero, Sage, NetSuite and SAP Business One, and imports from Procore and Autodesk Construction Cloud, each enabled by the hub.
Meter external calls and show their cost to the hub.
acceptance: An unknown export outcome is reconciled, never re-sent blindly (test).
Imports create private records only (test).
Exports contain only the exporting company's own data (negative tests).

packages.title: Procurement analytics without surveillance
packages.goal: Give companies spend, price history, supplier performance from own records, requisition fulfilment, cycle times and team throughput, with a self-view for each person and no individual rankings.
steps: Read-only views over the procurement ledgers and records the company participates in.
Team cells below three people collapse into the company total; a personal self-view; consent-based sharing of one's own figures.
Report drafts for the agent and a scoped export of the company's own data.
acceptance: No endpoint returns a metric per person to anyone but that person without a recorded consent (negative tests).
No other company's private data enters any figure (test).

packages.title: Plan to procurement: takeoffs, demand schedules and plan-change flags
packages.goal: Turn approved plan items into takeoffs, a demand schedule and requisition drafts, and flag linked requisitions, RFQs and orders when a plan change touches their items.
steps: Migration for takeoff; takeoff lines with sources from manual entry, spreadsheets or a takeoff extension.
Demand schedule from plan dates minus known lead times (own history or offering availability only).
Flag stale_reason plan_changed on linked records when a plan change is approved; never cancel automatically.
acceptance: Takeoff quantities stay estimates until a person confirms them (test).
A plan change flags every linked requisition, RFQ and order (test).
Lead times never use another company's private data (test).

packages.title: Delivery coordination: site logistics, delivery slots and resource booking
packages.goal: Coordinate deliveries with site access windows, slot proposals, crane, hoist and loading-bay bookings and just-in-time call-offs from the plan schedule.
steps: Migrations for site_logistics_profile, site_resource and delivery_slot with an exclusion constraint against double booking.
Share logistics profiles only with suppliers holding an accepted order.
Propose just-in-time call-off dates from plan dates and lead times.
acceptance: Resource bookings never overlap (concurrency test).
Site addresses and access instructions reach only suppliers with an accepted order (negative tests).

packages.title: Price indices and escalation alerts
packages.goal: Import public or licensed price-index series as sourced datasets, support index-linked price adjustment clauses, and alert owners when indices move beyond thresholds for open commitments and budgets.
steps: Migrations for price_index_series, price_index_observation and escalation_watch.
Pipelines through the source registry with licence flags; revisions append.
Alerts as decisions waiting with the series, period and computation shown.
Serve index series and escalation computations to the supplier's private pricing workbook (BID-004).
acceptance: Series without a licence allowing display are not shown (test).
Alerts never reveal one company's commitments to another (negative test).
Escalation computed for one company's workbook never appears in another company's alerts or statistics (negative test).

packages.title: Warranty registration and handover registers
packages.goal: Create warranty registrations from receipts, installation acceptance and manufacturer warranty terms, flow them into the homeowner's home passport, and give companies an asset handover register.
steps: Migrations for warranty_registration and asset_register_entry.
Draft registrations from accepted receipts and acceptance records; register with a manufacturer only with the owner's consent.
Link registrations to home passport installed items (HOME-001) and to the company handover register.
acceptance: Registrations stay owner-private and never federate (negative tests).
No manufacturer receives a registration without the owner's consent (test).

packages.title: Anonymized price benchmarks and lead-time signals (opt-in, off by default)
packages.goal: Publish hub-level price and lead-time aggregates from opted-in companies' accepted historical prices only, with minimum groups, a dominance limit and a time lag, after counsel sign-off per hub.
steps: Migrations for benchmark_contribution_consent and price_benchmark.
Compute cells per material class, unit, region and quarter from accepted agreement prices older than the lag; suppress cells below five buyers and five sellers or above the dominance share.
Refuse activation in a hub without a recorded counsel sign-off; show method, period and group size beside every figure.
acceptance: Suppression rules hold for every cell (property tests).
No current RFQ, quote or identity enters any input (test).
Withdrawing consent excludes the company from future periods (test).

packages.title: Embodied carbon from product EPDs
packages.goal: Attach environmental product declaration data to product entries and offerings, show embodied carbon in bid levelling and project totals, and label sources and validity honestly.
steps: Migration for product_epd with programme operator, standard, declared unit, GWP for modules A1 to A3, validity and licence.
Collect from manufacturers who claimed their page and from licensed EPD sources; never scrape behind a login.
Optional carbon column in levelling and project totals with units converted through the unit catalogue.
acceptance: Expired EPDs are labelled and excluded from totals unless the person includes them (test).
No carbon figure is shown as verified by the platform (test).

packages.title: Surplus and returns exchange
packages.goal: List leftover stock as surplus offerings with pickup terms, answer requests through the normal quote and agreement flow, and prepare returns to suppliers, without logistics or held funds.
steps: Offering kind surplus linked to stock movements surplus_listed and surplus_sold (catalogue extension agreed with the integrator).
Pickup coordination through context threads and delivery slots; payment only through providers or recorded externally.
Returns to suppliers through supplier_return records.
acceptance: Surplus listings never reveal the site address before an accepted agreement (negative test).
Surplus listings rank like any offering, never by payment (comparison test).

packages.title: Opt-in demand pooling for small contractors
packages.goal: Let a participant organizer pool small contractors' demand for one sourcing event under competition-law guard rails, with each member contracting and paying separately and no member seeing another.
steps: Migrations for demand_pool and pool_commitment.
Guard rails: purchasing only, free exit before award, no exchange of members' selling prices or customers, hub maximum share, counsel sign-off before the hub enables pooling.
Award creates one agreement per member at the pooled terms.
acceptance: Members never see each other's identities, quantities or terms (negative tests).
No funds are pooled: each member pays the supplier through its own agreement (test).
Pooling cannot be enabled without the counsel record (test).

packages.title: Procurement and supply entries in the shared capability registry (agent parity)
packages.goal: Apply ADR 010 decision 23 to the suite: every procurement and supply operation is registered once in the shared capability registry that the agent runtime, MCP connections and the interface use, with kind, inputs and outputs, data classes, mandate action, confirmation policy and meter, and the CI parity report shows no gap.
steps: Register the entries of capabilities.ts in the shared capability registry; until an engine-wide registry package exists, serve them from this module behind the same interface.
Bind each capability to one use case; the web route and the agent tool call the same use case.
Enforce humanOnly capabilities as decision cards confirmed on the first-party surface; connections can propose but never confirm them.
acceptance: A parity test fails when a capability lacks a web route or an agent tool, or when a route or tool lacks a capability (test).
humanOnly capabilities cannot be pre-authorized by any mandate or extension (test).

packages.title: Procurement on the web: requisitions, approvals, supplier base, sourcing and levelling
packages.goal: Build the buyer-side procurement screens on the API: requisitions with imports and progress, approvals as decision cards, the private supplier base and cards, sourcing events with levelling sheets, awards and outcome notices.
steps: Reach every screen from the existing Procurement destination and from projects; approvals appear in decisions waiting; no new top-level navigation and no generic inbox.
Requisition form, CSV and XLSX import with row errors, line progress; levelling sheet with pinned versions, adjustments and exclusions; award and notices.
Strings in a procurement namespace in every engine language; dates, numbers and money through Intl.
acceptance: Stale quotes are visibly non-comparable; adjustments are labelled buyer estimates.
Mobile, keyboard, screen reader, empty, error and denial states verified; levelling usable at 375 px with a wide-screen hint.
Every screen action maps to a capability of the parity registry (test).

packages.title: Supply on the web: receiving (mobile, offline), stock, invoices, payments, budgets and analytics
packages.goal: Build the supply screens on the API: offline receiving with photos, stock and transfers, invoices with match exceptions, payment proposals with payee warnings, budgets with planned, committed and actual, and analytics with self-view.
steps: Receiving works offline through the mobile web layer of CHAN-001 and shows device and server times.
Invoice and payment screens show match results, risk signals and payee change warnings prominently; release requires the approval state.
Analytics shows team-level figures and a personal self-view only; strings in a supply namespace in every engine language.
acceptance: No screen shows a per-person metric about someone else (test).
Payee details appear masked only; no screen accepts bank details outside the provider form (test).
Mobile, keyboard, screen reader, offline, empty, error and denial states verified.

packages.title: Console: procurement and supply settings
packages.goal: Add the procurement and supply section of the hub console: approval route templates, document types and requirement-set templates, e-invoicing networks, integrations, AI intake settings, tolerance and fraud-control defaults, benchmark and pooling policy, unit conversions; first on fixtures, then live.
steps: Screen HC-68 at /modules/procurement on fixtures, then wired to hub configuration domain procurement and provider connections.
Second-person activation for fraud-control, benchmark and pooling policy and for live adapters; counsel record required for benchmarks and pooling.
Strings under admin.modules.procurement in every engine language.

Add bid desk settings to the procurement section: module enablement, tender sources with recorded terms, extraction routes and meters, scorecard, review and teaming templates, approval route templates for bid_decision and bid_submission, the per-country competition-law note and retention classes.
acceptance: No company's routes, suppliers, budgets, invoices, stock or payments are readable without a case grant (negative tests).
Fraud-control values below the engine minimum are rejected (test).
Cohort counts below ten companies are suppressed (test).
Staff never see pursuits, workbooks or tender documents without a case grant (negative test).

packages.title: Console component kit in packages/ui
packages.goal: Give every console section one accessible set of shared components: data grid mode of DataTable (server-side sorting, filtering and pagination, selection, column visibility, saved views slot), filter bar with active-filter chips, facet panel, saved views, bulk-action bar, non-modal detail drawer, audit trail, diff viewer, approval card, permission matrix, scope picker, effective access, locked rule, typed confirmation, step-up prompt, reason field, command palette, inbox list, inline help, keyboard shortcuts, run history, calendar agenda, a metric chart with its data table and the network map (component level).
steps: Extend DataTable backward-compatibly with a controlled server-side mode and selection; add the new components with stories and unit tests.

Promote the console compositions that are reused (StatusLabel, ReasonField, AuditNote, ApprovalCard, KillSwitchControl, CohortCount, money cells, run history) from apps/web/app/admin/_components without breaking ADM-002 screens.
Strings in packages/ui/locales for every engine language; axe and keyboard tests for every component at 1280, 768 and 375 px.
acceptance: The permission matrix and editable grids follow the APG grid keyboard model; read-only lists stay tables (tested).
The step-up prompt and typed confirmation accept paste and password managers (WCAG 3.3.8); no component relies on colour alone or on dragging (tests).
Selection, filter and result counts are announced in polite live regions; the detail drawer returns focus to the row it was opened from.
The metric chart and the network map are always paired with an equivalent table or list; the network map loads no third-party tiles and never shows a restricted place as selectable (tests).

packages.title: Dark theme tokens
packages.goal: Add a dark token set with the same custom-property names under [data-theme="dark"], a system, light or dark preference, and contrast evidence for both themes, starting with the console.
steps: Define dark values for every colour role, status family, focus ring, overlay and scrim; components keep referencing roles only.
Extend the token contrast unit tests to the dark set; add the preference (system default) to the console shell and the design-system showcase.
Screenshots of every console component in both themes at 1280 and 375 px.
acceptance: Every text and status token meets 4.5:1 (3:1 for large text, control boundaries and the focus ring) in both themes (unit test).
Status is never shown by colour alone in either theme; the console header band stays distinct from page content in both themes.

packages.title: Staff lifecycle and access governance backend
packages.goal: Complete staff management without weakening ADM-001: invitations with expiry and second-person approval for sensitive roles, assignments with end dates, eligible roles activated just in time with a fresh second factor and approval, access-review campaigns, guided offboarding, an effective-access query and a role-change preview with the separation-of-duties check.
steps: Add a staff-lifecycle contract (invitation, eligible assignment, activation request, access review campaign and item, offboarding record, effective access, role-change preview) in its own file; request any change to hub.ts or admin.ts from the integrator.

Implement invitations, eligible roles and activation through DATA-002-style SECURITY DEFINER commands that reuse the existing approval, conflict and audit rules; activation length bounded per role and never above BREAKGLASS_MAX_HOURS.

Implement access-review campaigns (reviewer differs from holder, unanswered items escalate to the hub owner, never silent removal) and offboarding that revokes roles, eligible roles, pending approvals and admin clients in one transaction and lists open work for reassignment.
Implement the effective-access query and the role-change preview that the API recomputes at apply time.
acceptance: Nobody invites, assigns, activates or reviews themselves; an invitation or activation for a sensitive role cannot take effect without a second person (negative tests on real PostgreSQL under the runtime role).
An activation ends at its window end without a job having to run (checked at every request); a revoked role ends elevations, eligible roles, pending approvals and grants at once (tested).
A role change whose preview is stale is refused; in full separation-of-duties mode a conflicting role is refused (tested).
No endpoint returns activity, productivity or behaviour metrics about a staff member (schema walk).

Invitations may name a function position; offboarding cannot complete while the person owns a function or is accountable for an agent role and offers the hub owner as fallback, who must accept; an abrupt role loss suspends the affected agent roles at once (tested).

packages.title: Console search, saved views, approvals inbox and flag rollout backend
packages.goal: Serve the console navigation layer: a permission-aware search over console objects (sections, approvals, configuration versions, incidents, cases by id, runs, audit events, flags, staff) that never searches participant data, saved views per person and per team, one read model of work assigned to a staff member, notification preferences, and rollout stages for feature flags.
steps: Add a console-services contract (search query and hits, saved view, work item, notification preference, flag rollout stage) in its own file.
Implement search that resolves each hit through the owning read permission and answers identical "nothing found" for missing and unreadable objects.

Implement the work-item read model from approvals, case grants, recovery escalations, access reviews, cases, appeals, incidents, alerts and Agent team review items, each with the reason it is the viewer's.
Extend flags with stages (off, staff only, a deterministic share of sessions, on) without changing the rule that flags never touch access, projections, egress or ranking.
acceptance: No search request or response contains participant personal data; participant lookup stays in the support workspace with a case and an access-log entry (schema walk and negative tests).
A staff member never receives a work item or search hit for an object they may not read (negative tests per role and scope).
Turning a flag off is immediate; a flag stage cannot target individual people (tested).

packages.title: Console navigation layer on fixtures: command palette, approvals inbox, saved views, shortcuts and the Users area home
packages.goal: Build the cross-cutting navigation of the console on fixtures: the command palette (Ctrl or Cmd+K) that navigates and opens command forms but never searches participants, the approvals inbox (/inbox), saved views, keyboard shortcuts that can be turned off, notification preferences, and the Users area home with tabs for people, companies, staff and clients.
steps: Build the palette, the inbox, saved views, shortcuts and the Users area home in their own folders with fixtures validated by the contracts.
Add the console-navigation namespace in every engine language.
Playwright and axe at 1280, 768 and 375 px; wire to ADM-005 when it is done.
acceptance: Typing an e-mail or a name in the palette offers only "Look up a participant in Support" and never shows participant data (test).
The inbox approves and declines at 375 px with the diff as a list of changed fields; own requests cannot be approved (test).
Single-character shortcuts can be turned off and never fire inside text fields (WCAG 2.1.4, test).
The Users area home opens participants only through their public projection or the support lookup with a case, staff through their staff page and clients through their client page (test).

packages.title: Console Agent team area on fixtures
packages.goal: Build the Agent team area of ADR 010 decision 26 on fixtures: roster, roles with capabilities from the registry, operator grants, autonomy levels on the same scale as the editorial agent team, runs, the review queue, budgets and evaluations, kill switches per agent and per role, and the human-only decisions shown as locked rows.
steps: Build HC-200 to HC-206 with fixtures for the platform-wide roles; list the editorial roles of EDIT-002 read-only with links to Editorial → Team (HC-184 … HC-189); every agent output labelled as agent work.
Add the agent-team namespace in every engine language.
Playwright and axe at 1280, 768 and 375 px.
acceptance: Enable stays blocked without a passing evaluation; widening a grant with a data class or commit capability shows the second-person requirement (fixtures).
No control lets an operator agent decide a human-only decision; those appear as locked rows with explanations (scan).
Every agent shows its accountable person; an agent without one shows as suspended.
The roster and roles screens filter by function and show the function owner; a function without an owner shows its agents as paused with the reason (fixtures).

packages.title: Console Statistics area on fixtures
packages.goal: Build the mandatory Statistics area (HC-210 to HC-215) on fixtures and wire it to ANL-001 when it is done: dashboards per domain, the metric catalogue with definitions, segments and funnels, reports and scheduled exports, access and retention settings, and metric detail, all as cohort aggregates.
steps: Build the screens with synthetic, labelled fixtures validated by the contracts; every chart with its data table.
Add the console-statistics namespace in every engine language.
Playwright and axe at 1280, 768 and 375 px in both themes; wire to ANL-001 when it is done.
acceptance: No screen, filter, drill-down or export leads to one participant or one staff member (scan and test).
Counts under ten after segmentation render as "fewer than 10" and secondary suppression hides revealing cells (test).
Money flows are labelled as recorded instructions to the licensed payment provider; a metric whose source is not live shows its status label, not a number (test).
Each dashboard is visible only to the roles its catalogue entry names (negative test per persona).
Statistics dashboards can be filtered by function and are linked from the function dashboards (TEAM-006).

packages.title: Operator agent team: roles, operator grants, autonomy levels, budgets, evaluation gate and kill switches
packages.goal: Give the hub operator an internal team of agents (ADR 010 decision 26): hub-owned agent principals, role definitions over the one capability registry, structured and revocable operator grants, an autonomy level per role, an accountable staff member per role, schedules, budgets with hard stops, model routes, an evaluation gate before enabling, kill switches per agent and per role, run history and a review queue, all audited.
steps: Add an operator-agents contract (role definition, operator grant, autonomy level, agent, run, review item) in its own file; request the additive hub.ts change for kill-switch scopes per operator agent and per role from the integrator.
Implement operator principals that act only under operator grants, never under a participant mandate, and suspend when the role has no accountable staff member.
Run the EVAL-001 safety suite and role checks before enabling and after any model, grant or role change; enforce budgets and kill switches before every capability call.
Feed review items to the console work list (ADM-005) and write every action to the audit with the agent, grant and accountable person.

Share one operator principal kind, one grant model, one autonomy scale and one set of kill-switch scopes with the editorial agent team (EDIT-002), coordinating the contract with it instead of defining a second model.
acceptance: Sanctions and screening decisions, account suspensions and sanctions, money and commitments, appeals, legal holds, claim and link decisions, price activation and every HUMAN_GATES decision are unreachable for operator agents at every autonomy level (negative tests).
An operator agent never reads or changes a participant's agent, mandates, settings or conversations, and never acts as a participant or a staff member (negative tests).
An exhausted budget or an engaged kill switch stops queued and running work; release needs a second person and an incident note (tested).
Every output is labelled as agent work; no output, run or statistic carries per-person behaviour analytics.

Every agent role belongs to one function of the operating company (functionKey); kill switches exist per function as well as per agent and per role; an agent can never be a function owner, position holder, approver or reviewer, nor counted for launch gates or separation of duties (negative tests); the stored autonomy scale is the one of the hub operating company chapter (Off, Observe, Draft, Act with review, Act within limits) with a separate trigger.

packages.title: Supply agent modules: requisition desk, sourcing desk, intake, receiving clerk, payables desk, supply watch, surplus exchange
packages.goal: Ship the Supply family of agent modules so a person's one agent can do every procurement and supply operation within mandates: draft requisitions and RFQs, chase replies, level bids, process documents, record receipts, prepare and release payments, watch budgets, indices and documents.
steps: Module manifests with jobs, triggers, mandate templates, meters and locale keys for every engine language.
Use only the parity registry capabilities; approvals, acceptance and risk-signal clearance stay human_only.
Safety suite: document injection, payee-change attempts through documents and other agents, competitor price disclosure, reminder quotas.
Keep buyer-side supply modules and the supplier bid desk separated inside a company that both buys and bids: sourcing desk data never feeds a pursuit and pursuit data never feeds sourcing.
acceptance: No module can approve, clear a risk signal or change a payee (tests).
Competing suppliers never receive each other's prices or participation (test).
release_payment respects the cooling-off period and open risk signals under every approval policy (test).
A company that is both buyer and bidder on related work cannot read its buyer-side levelling data from a pursuit or the reverse (negative test).

packages.title: Fair subscription controls: disclosure, renewal reminders, easy cancellation, price-change notice
packages.goal: Make every paid hub plan as easy to leave as to join: recurring price before purchase, renewal reminders, online cancellation, no termination fees, notice and grandfathering for price increases, no silently expiring credits; the engine refuses plan versions that break these rules.
steps: Add plan-version rules (renewal reminder lead time, cancellation path, notice period, credit validity disclosure) as validated fields of subscription plan and offer versions.
Implement renewal reminders through notification templates in every hub language and online cancellation that takes effect at the end of the paid period.
Apply price increases only from the payer's next renewal after the notice period; keep accepted versions unchanged.
Refuse activation of plan or credit-pack versions without disclosed validity and refund policy; record the version shown at purchase.
acceptance: A plan version without a renewal reminder, an online cancellation path or a notice period cannot be activated (test).
Cancellation takes no more steps than purchase, measured on the flow definition; no early-termination fee can be configured.
A price increase never applies to a payer before the notice period and the next renewal (test with clock).
Credits never expire without a validity shown before purchase; unknown payment outcomes reconcile, never double-charge.

packages.title: Review integrity controls and the public review policy
packages.goal: Keep reviews trustworthy under laws such as the US FTC reviews rule and the UK DMCC Act: reviews only from counterparties of recorded work, no incentives or sentiment gating, no suppression, spike locks, a public review policy and an internal evidence log of the steps taken.
steps: Validate review eligibility against recorded agreements, tasks or consultations; label and exclude unconfirmed reviews from aggregates.
Detect spikes, rings and reciprocal patterns and open moderation cases; never apply automatic sanctions or silent score changes.
Record every integrity step (checks, cases, decisions) in an append-only log exportable to the hub for regulators.
Publish the review policy page in every hub language from versioned hub text.
acceptance: A review without a recorded relationship is rejected (negative test).
No code path offers an incentive for a review or filters review requests by expected sentiment (test).
A fair negative review cannot be hidden by the reviewed party or by payment; responses and disputes are the only paths.
The policy page renders in every engine language with its version and date.

packages.title: Ranking statements generated from configuration for every ranked surface
packages.goal: Publish, for every ranked surface (directory, matching, needs board, search, recommendations, event listings), the main ranking parameters and the statement that payment has no influence, generated from the active method versions and hub configuration so it can never drift.
steps: Define a ranking-statement contract per surface derived from match, recommendation and search method versions.
Render the public statements page in every hub language and link it from each ranked list.
Regenerate statements on every method or configuration activation and keep the history.
acceptance: Changing a method version changes the published statement in the same activation (test).
Every ranked surface links to its statement; the statement says that payment, plans and sponsorship do not influence ranking, and tests prove it.
The page renders in every engine language.

packages.title: Named-performer confirmation on offers, quotes and work records
packages.goal: Stop identity borrowing: when an offer, quote or work record names a licensed or certified person, that person confirms it from their own account; until then the name shows as not confirmed.
steps: Add a named-performer reference to offer, quote and work-record versions with a confirmation request to the named person.
Show "named performer confirmed" or "not confirmed" in every projection that shows the name; never upgrade a licence badge from the name alone.
Let country packs mark categories where confirmation is required before acceptance.
acceptance: A named person who did not confirm is shown as not confirmed everywhere (projection test).
Only the named person's own account can confirm (negative test with another member of the same company).
Withdrawn confirmation after acceptance is recorded and shown to the counterparty without changing the accepted version.

packages.title: Badge and label vocabulary guard
packages.goal: Prevent misleading trust wording: badge and label texts in every locale use a fixed, counsel-reviewed vocabulary, and the words certified, licensed, guaranteed and approved (and their translations) appear only in keys bound to a register fact or a recorded accreditation.
steps: List the restricted words per engine language and the locale keys allowed to use them.
Add a check that scans locale namespaces and fails on restricted words outside allowed keys.
Document the vocabulary for translators and hub operators.
acceptance: The check fails on a restricted word in an unapproved key in any engine language (test with fixtures).
Allowed keys are tied to sourced or accredited facts in their component contracts.
Adding a language without its restricted-word list fails the check.

packages.title: Worker credential card: holder-presented, offline-verifiable credentials
packages.goal: Give workers a credential card on their phone (identity check level, trainings, licences) that a site, an event or a client verifies offline against the issuing node's key and status list, without the engine ever logging verifications as attendance or location.
steps: Package selected passport credentials into a QR presentation with short validity and selective disclosure where the format supports it.
Provide an offline verifier page that checks signatures and a cached status list.
Show the holder exactly what a verifier sees before presenting.
acceptance: Verification works offline with a status list fetched within its validity (test).
The engine stores no record of who verified whose card, where or when (negative test on audit and logs).
A revoked credential fails verification after the next status list refresh.

packages.title: EU trader traceability for consumer-facing offers
packages.goal: In EU hubs, collect and make best efforts to verify trader traceability information before a trader can offer to consumers, show trader or non-trader status on offers, and let traders meet their information duties (Digital Services Act Articles 30 and 31).
steps: Add traceability fields and verification states from the EU layer of the country packs.
Block consumer-facing offers of traders without complete traceability; show trader status on offers.
Provide a suspension and notice path when information proves inaccurate.
acceptance: A trader without complete traceability cannot publish a consumer-facing offer in an EU hub (test).
Non-EU hubs are unaffected unless their pack enables the facet.
Trader status shows on every consumer-facing offer projection.
A consumer-facing offer from another hub shown in an EU hub carries trader traceability from its home node, or is not shown to consumers (tested).

packages.title: Wallet-based identity and attribute verification
packages.goal: Let people prove identity and professional attributes with digital identity wallets (EU Digital Identity Wallet, mobile driver's licences, national eID where a hub enables them) through an adapter with a fake, storing verification results and claims, never raw credentials.
steps: Define the verification-level contract (email_verified, document_checked, wallet_verified, in_person) with issuer and date.
Add a relying-party adapter port with a deterministic fake and per-country configuration from packs.
Record results as evidence usable by claims and credentials; show categories, never documents.

National digital identity checks used in the launch countries (for example Ghana Card, PhilSys, NIN, Maisha Namba, MyID) run only through licensed verification providers configured per hub, minimised to a result, a level, the issuer and a date.
acceptance: No raw credential or document is stored (test).
A wallet presentation from a restricted place is refused.
Verification results appear in projections only as categories and dates.
No national identity number, document image or biometric is stored; only the verification result, level, issuer and date (test).

packages.title: Tender source adapters, Open Contracting first
packages.goal: Import public tenders and awards from national portals (SAM.gov, the UK Central Digital Platform, TED, Brazil's PNCP, Chile's Mercado Publico, India's GeM and others) through adapters that map to the Open Contracting Data Standard, each with licence flags and a fake. The launch-country portals of the launch playbooks are added on top of this mapping by PROC-003.
steps: Define an OCDS-based mapping contract for notices and awards.
Add adapters with fakes and recorded fixtures per portal family; register each as a source with licence flags.
Feed notices to the opportunities board and awards to sourced track records.

Record per portal the automated-access and redistribution terms (CTRY-004 automated_access_terms); use only official APIs or bulk data with a hub-held system account key from KEYS-001; fetch notice attachments only where the terms allow redistribution.
Map eForms and OCDS submission deadlines, enquiry periods, lots, award criteria and the electronic-submission address to structured fields of the notice contract.
acceptance: No adapter submits bids or contacts buyers (test).
A portal whose terms forbid reuse cannot be activated as a source.
Imported notices are labelled from a public source and never appear as platform members' needs.
Imported notices federate only as link_only unless the source licence allows redisplay, and keep their ocid as an external identifier (tested).
No adapter uses or stores a participant's personal portal login (test).
Attachments of a portal whose terms forbid redistribution are never served to participants (test).

packages.title: Electronic signature adapters bound to agreement digests
packages.goal: Let parties sign agreements, acts and waivers with electronic signatures valid in their jurisdiction (ESIGN and UETA providers in the US, eIDAS advanced and qualified signatures in the EU, national schemes elsewhere) through adapters with fakes; the signed document's hash binds to the agreement digest.
steps: Define the signature request and evidence contracts with signature level and provider reference.
Add an adapter port with a deterministic fake; per-country signature levels come from packs.
Reconcile unknown provider outcomes; never resend blindly.
acceptance: A signature over a document whose hash differs from the agreement digest is rejected (test).
Signature levels shown match the pack facts for the parties' jurisdictions.
Unknown outcomes go to reconciliation (fault-injection test).
Recognition of the other party's signature scheme across jurisdictions is shown only from a pack fact, otherwise as unknown (tested).

packages.title: Open BIM exchange for product data and plan items (IFC property sets)
packages.goal: Export and import product entries and plan items as IFC property sets so designers can use Trustwork product data in their BIM tools, without shipping proprietary formats.
steps: Map product entry and plan-step attributes to IFC property sets with the taxonomy crosswalk slots.
Add export and import endpoints with validation and provenance per field.
Document the mapping and its limits.
acceptance: Exports validate against the pinned IFC schema version (test).
Imports never overwrite sourced or claimed facts without provenance.
No proprietary classification ships in the repository.

packages.title: Installable, offline-first mobile web shell
packages.goal: Make the web app installable and dependable on site: manifest and offline shell, encrypted offline caches cleared on sign-out, low-data and sunlight-readable modes, and web push only with permission per category.
steps: Add the web app manifest and an offline shell that never caches other people's data.
Add low-data and high-contrast large-target preferences in every engine language.
Add web push with per-category permission and quiet hours.

Honour the Save-Data request header and the low-data preference on public pages: text first, images on demand, no client JavaScript needed to read an article, a company page or an event (launch playbooks: Kenya, Nigeria, Rwanda and rural areas everywhere).
acceptance: Signing out or losing access clears offline caches at the next sync (test).
The shell works offline for assigned items only (browser test).
Push is never sent without permission for that category.
In low-data mode the public article, company and event pages stay within a documented transfer budget on a throttled 3G profile and remain readable without client JavaScript (browser test).

packages.title: Accessibility programme: manual audits and a per-hub accessibility statement
packages.goal: Turn WCAG 2.2 AA from a target into recorded evidence: manual walkthroughs per release with screen readers, keyboard, zoom and reduced motion, and an accessibility statement per hub generated from that evidence with a barrier-report contact.
steps: Define the audit record (device, assistive technology, steps, evidence, issues, reviewer) and a release checklist.
Generate the hub accessibility statement page from recorded evidence in every hub language.
Add the brand-overlay contrast check as a launch gate input.
acceptance: The statement never claims conformance beyond recorded evidence (test on generator).
A release without a manual audit record is flagged in the release checklist.
The statement page renders in every engine language.

packages.title: Privacy-preserving analytics: own metrics, cohorts and aggregate readership
packages.goal: Give participants their own metrics and hubs cohort analytics without surveillance: first-party aggregate events with short raw retention, cohorts of at least ten, no third-party trackers, honoured opt-outs and Global Privacy Control.
steps: Define event and cohort contracts with suppression below the minimum cohort.
Aggregate in the worker; expire raw events quickly; expose own metrics to participants and cohorts to hub staff.
Honour opt-outs and Global Privacy Control where the law requires.
acceptance: No per-person behaviour view exists for staff (negative test).
Every count under ten is suppressed (test).
No third-party tracker or advertising identifier is loaded by any page (browser test).

A versioned metric catalogue (definition, formula, source projection, freshness, allowed segments, visibility roles, owner, status) backs every statistic the console shows (console design, section 7).
Suppression is applied after segmentation, with secondary suppression so that no total, period difference or sibling segment reveals a suppressed cell (tested with differencing probes).

Funnels are counted by entry cohort and show a conversion only when both steps have at least ten; exports and scheduled reports are signed, suppressed, audited and sent only to staff who hold the permission when the report is sent (tests).
The metric catalogue carries the function KPIs of the hub operating company chapter as cohort metrics with an owning function; no metric about an individual staff member exists (schema walk).

packages.title: Data-broker readiness and deletion-platform adapters
packages.goal: Before a hub enables people data from sources, check whether it may be a data broker under applicable law, record registrations, and process state deletion platforms (for example California's DROP) through an adapter with a fake.
steps: Add a broker-status checklist that gates people datasets in the console.
Add a deletion-platform adapter port with a fake and scheduled retrieval within the legal cadence.
Apply deletions through privacy operations with the erasure ledger and tombstones.
acceptance: A people dataset cannot be activated without a recorded broker-status decision (test).
Deletion requests retrieved from the platform are applied and reported within the configured cadence (clock test).
Deletions propagate to indexes and peers as tombstones.

packages.title: Financing partner referrals: licensed, labelled, never ranking
packages.goal: Let a hub list licensed trade-credit and project-finance partners with disclosed referral fees, shown as labelled options to participants who ask, never influencing ranking, matching, recommendations or reputation, and never consumer lending unless the partner is licensed for it.
steps: Add financing partner records with licence evidence, jurisdictions, products and referral-fee disclosure.
Show partners only on request or in a labelled panel; never in candidate lists.
Screen partners with the compliance package before activation (second person).
acceptance: Rankings are identical with and without financing partners configured (comparison test).
A partner without recorded licence evidence for the jurisdiction cannot be activated.
Referral fees are shown before any referral.

packages.title: Pre-collection gate: AI-usage signals, TDM reservations, host policy and polite crawling
packages.goal: Decide before any request leaves the node whether a URL may be fetched and for which uses, combining source status, restricted places, access barriers, robots.txt (RFC 9309), recorded terms, legal basis, licence, RSL, IETF Content-Usage signals and TDMRep reservations, and record the decision with every run.
steps: Add contracts for the collection decision (allow, deny, wait with reason codes and narrowed allowed uses) and for AI-usage signals and host policy.

Implement the gate as a pure function plus a worker adapter that fetches and caches robots.txt (at most 24 hours, server errors mean disallow), RSL documents, TDMRep files and Content-Usage headers, each with digests.
Implement per-host politeness: one concurrent request by default, crawl delay, polite window, backoff on 429 and 503 honouring Retry-After, and a stable bot user agent with a contact page.
Detect login walls, paywalls and technical barriers and refuse collection behind them; pause the source on any signal digest change; schedule licence expiry re-checks.
Publish the hub's own outbound content terms as an RSL document.
acceptance: No request is sent for a URL whose decision is deny (network fake test asserting zero calls).
Unknown, unparsable or conflicting signals narrow allowed uses to the most restrictive reading (tests).
A changed robots, terms, RSL or TDMRep digest pauses the source until a person re-checks it.

packages.title: Translation memory, glossaries and post-editing workflow
packages.goal: Give each hub a translation memory, termbases per hub, topic and plan step, a machine translation and post-editing workflow with quality checks, a language-scoped reviewer role and per-locale publish gates, so linked editions are complete, labelled and never silently out of date.
steps: Add translation_memory_segment, termbase_entry, translation_job and translation_qa_result (packages/data/migrations/translation); add the language-scoped translator-reviewer staff role through the console contract minor version.
Implement the edition states requested, pretranslated, machine_draft, post_editing, qa_failed, in_review, approved, scheduled, published and stale; the reviewer is never the post-editor.

Apply TM exact and fuzzy matches (bands 95-99, 85-94, 75-84) before machine translation; only reviewed segments enter TM, credited to the reviewer; text whose licence forbids storing or translating, private data and quarantined text never enter TM.
Implement blocking QA checks (glossary, do-not-translate, numbers, dates, units, identifiers, links, placeholders, untranslated segments, script) and quality estimation as a routing signal only.
Mark editions stale when their original is corrected; support TMX and XLIFF 2.1 import and export; remove TM segments on source takedown.
acceptance: Unreviewed machine output never enters translation memory and never publishes without a named reviewer, except under an active standing policy after the owner confirms decision E3 (tests).
A correction of an original marks every edition stale and shows the notice in every engine language.
A segment from a taken-down source disappears from TM and from match results (test).

packages.title: Reader correction requests, notices, takedowns and statements of reasons
packages.goal: Let anyone submit a correction request or a notice about content (copyright, licence, legal, privacy, illegal content, source owner removal, right of reply), and let the hub acknowledge, decide, send a statement of reasons, offer a complaint path and apply the effect with tombstones.
steps: Add notice, notice_decision, statement_of_reasons and correction_request (packages/data/migrations/notices) with states received, acknowledged, triaged, decided, reasons_sent, complaint_open and closed.
Apply upheld decisions through the owning modules' use cases only: hold, correction, unpublishing, source record removal; emit retrieval, translation memory and federation tombstones.

Expose a public intake form and an acknowledgement; keep notifier identity out of what the affected author sees unless the hub's legal settings require it; aggregate counts for the transparency report.
acceptance: Every decided notice has a statement of reasons and the decision cites the rule applied (test).
An upheld source owner removal tombstones the source's records in indexes, translation memory and peers (integration test).
Notice data never appears in public projections or analytics rows (negative test).

packages.title: Newsletters and distribution channels
packages.goal: Send newsletter editions that reference published versions, with double opt-in, one-click unsubscribe and no tracking pixels, and record the publication state of each item per channel (site, feeds, newsletter, magazine, agent knowledge, peers).
steps: Add newsletter, newsletter_subscription, newsletter_edition and channel_publication (packages/data/migrations/distribution); editions pin publication versions and refuse an item that lost its approval or was retracted.
Send through the communications outbox and mail adapter with idempotency keys and one-click unsubscribe (RFC 8058); corrections to sent items appear as notices in the next edition.
Show per-channel status for every publication and count reads only as suppressed aggregates.
acceptance: No newsletter contains an open-tracking pixel or a per-recipient tracking parameter (test).
A retracted or embargoed item cannot be included in an edition (test).
An unknown send outcome is reconciled, never resent blindly.

packages.title: Media library with rights, alt text and provenance
packages.goal: Keep every image and file used in content with its rights holder, licence, permitted uses, expiry, credit line, alt text in each hub language, IPTC digital source type, C2PA manifest reference and a where-used list, so a withdrawn or expired licence can be acted on everywhere.
steps: Add media_asset, media_rights, media_alt_text and media_usage (packages/data/migrations/media) on top of the object storage port.
Refuse approval of a publication whose images lack alt text (or a decorative mark) or whose licence does not permit the use; alert before licence expiry.
Keep AI-generated images labelled and block their use in documentary placements (news lead images of real events, company products, project pages).
acceptance: Withdrawing an asset lists and replaces or removes every use (test).
An AI-generated image cannot be attached to a documentary placement (negative test).

packages.title: Editorial agent team: roles, autonomy per role and content class, and standing publication policies
packages.goal: Implement the owner decision of 2026-11-01: an internal team of AI roles (scout, collector, researcher, writer, fact-checker, translator, post-editor, editor-assistant, layout, designer, illustrator, photo researcher, metadata, distribution, curator, licence, accessibility, corrections watch, knowledge packager) with registry capabilities, model routes, caps, schedules, quality floors and an autonomy level per role and content class, plus standing publication policies for the eligible classes only.
steps: Write ADR 015 (status proposed) on the editorial agent team and standing publication policies and the console contract minor version 1.1.0 (new permissions, second-person actions, roles); no code relies on standing policies before the ADR is accepted.
Register each role's read and draft capabilities in the capability registry with staff-only surfaces; no role capability has the publication side effect.

Add editorial_role_settings, standing_publication_policy and role_quality_record (packages/data/migrations/editorial-team); autonomy levels off, draft_only, auto_with_review and auto_publish_allowed per role and content class, with locked classes enforced by schema refinements.

Let the content module publish an item under a standing policy only when its class, conditions, limits and the policy's activation by a second person hold; record the policy, signer and activator on the publication; sample audits per policy.
Lower autonomy automatically (never raise it) when a quality floor is crossed, a kill switch is engaged, the model route changes version or the accountable editor-in-chief is gone.
acceptance: No path publishes news, a first publication, content naming a company or person with a claim, a correction changing a number, name, date or conclusion, or a magazine release without an individual review decision (negative tests).
A standing policy signed and activated by the same person, expired, or outside its class or limits publishes nothing (tests).
Bylines of automated pieces name the editorial office, the role names and the responsible editor; no role has a human name or portrait (fixture scan).
Without a named editor-in-chief every role and standing policy pauses (test).

packages.title: Console live wiring: editorial team, translation, notices, channels and media
packages.goal: Wire the editorial office screens added in HUBC-003 (team, standing policies, translation workbench, glossary and memory, notices, corrections, channels, media, licences, collection jobs, analytics and coverage) to the live API.
steps: Replace the fixture adapter for the new editorial sections with the API adapter, keeping the same contract types.
Route every second-person action (standing policy activation, autonomy raise, naming the editor-in-chief, legal unpublishing) through the approvals inbox.
Playwright and axe journeys in at least one non-English language on desktop and phone.
acceptance: Activating a standing policy or raising a role to auto-publish without a second person is refused against the API.
Analytics screens render no per-reader or per-staff row (DOM and network scan).

packages.title: Outreach and collection policy as country-pack facts and hub configuration
packages.goal: Express every country's outreach and data-collection regime as data (ADR 017, owner confirmation of 2026-11-01): an outreachLaw pack facet with sourced facts and a versioned hub outreach configuration domain, resolved most-protective-first, with an engine floor no setting can lower and strict as the default.
steps: Contracts in packages/contracts/src/outreach-policy.ts: recipient classes, channels, bases (prohibited, prior_consent, prior_express_written_consent, soft_opt_in, implied_consent_conspicuous_publication, legitimate_interest_assessed, opt_out, existing_relationship, single_consent_request), notice timing, identification, opt-out, volume, quiet hours, language order, registrations, retention and residency; the hub outreach domain with mode strict, notice_only or governed.

The outreachLaw facet schema in packages/country-packs/src/outreach-law.ts (registered additively in the facet list with the integrator's agreement), each fact with sources, verification level and counselReview; facts for the us, uz, ge, am and az packs and the EU layer, all counselReview pending.

Resolver: engine floor, recipient-jurisdiction pack rule, hub-jurisdiction pack rule, hub policy, source allowed uses and recipient suppression intersected; unknown jurisdiction or recipient class resolves to no contact.

Schema refinements: any mode other than strict needs a counsel approval reference and a second-person approval; consumer outreach, automated calls, AI voice, SMS or messenger outreach without prior consent, guessed addresses and missing identification cannot be expressed.
Propose outreach_policy_activation and outreach_campaign_activation as additive HUMAN_GATES entries with the integrator's agreement.
acceptance: A hub with no outreach configuration resolves every recipient to no contact (test).
No configuration can enable consumer outreach or automated calls, AI voice, SMS or messenger outreach without prior consent (schema test).
When two jurisdictions apply, the most protective rule wins (resolver test with the worked examples).
Every outreachLaw fact cites a source and shows counselReview; no engine code branches on a country code (test).

packages.title: Canonical entities, cited fields, sourced page assembly and change watch
packages.goal: Turn linked records into canonical entities (companies, events, projects, products, tenders, associations, training providers) whose every field cites its source, and publish them as sourced pages that never look verified, with freshness and change watch.
steps: Contracts in packages/contracts/src/sourced-pages.ts and tables canonical_entity, entity_member, entity_field, field_provenance, distinct_pair and change_event (packages/data/migrations/sourced-pages).
Field choice rules: registers for legal facts, the entity's own site for descriptive facts, claimed values over sourced ones, disagreement shown as words; confidence in words, never a score.
Model-extracted fields require an evidence span and allowed model egress for the source; no sensitive categories or private facts.
Page assembly per kind with the sourced label, a How this page was built panel and the claim, correct and remove actions; pages publish only through an activated import batch.
Change watch: register status, licence expiry, site availability, field TTL and peer tombstones; dissolved entities unpublish with tombstones.
acceptance: No sourced page shows a natural person's name or personal contact data, a rating, an activity counter or verification wording (projection test).
A model-extracted field without an evidence span is never stored (test).
A page is never public without an activated batch decision by a person (test).
Splitting an entity re-assembles the page from the remaining records and records the reason (test).

packages.title: Outreach orchestration: campaigns, gates, platform suppression, replies and deliverability
packages.goal: Contact representatives of sourced entities only where the resolved policy allows, through a gate chain that ends in the platform-wide suppression list, with honest messages, immediate opt-out, human hand-off of replies and deliverability discipline; strict mode sends nothing (ADR 017).
steps: Contracts in packages/contracts/src/outreach.ts and tables contact_point (encrypted value, provenance, basis, jurisdiction), legitimate_interest_assessment, outreach_campaign, outreach_campaign_version, outreach_touch, outreach_reply and do_not_collect_entry (packages/data/migrations/outreach); extend suppression_entry with scope and reasons with the communications owner's agreement.

Gate chain at planning and again at dispatch: policy mode, source contact use, recipient class and jurisdiction, basis, platform suppression (hub and node), restricted places and screening, caps and budgets, quiet hours, message checks, autonomy level and approvals; idempotency key per recipient and touch.

Templates with locked blocks (operator identification and postal address, automated assistant disclosure from HUB-005, data sources, page link, correct or remove, RFC 8058 one-click unsubscribe); sequences of at most three touches with fixed stop conditions.

Replies matched by reply token into an outreach_contact context thread, stored as untrusted; classification with ambiguity treated as objection; human hand-off queue; thread moves to the company context on verification.

Deliverability: separate outreach sender identity, DNS checks before start, complaint and bounce thresholds that pause campaigns, ramp caps; no open tracking; cohort metrics with counts under ten suppressed.
Agent team roles (drafter, sender, reply triager) act only under operator grants and approved campaign versions; kill switches per role, campaign, hub and node.
acceptance: With the hub policy in strict mode no code path sends to a non-participant (test across campaigns, agents, RFQ invitation notices and journeys).
A suppressed address receives nothing through any purpose, including when suppression lands while a batch is in flight (concurrency test on PostgreSQL).
No message leaves without every locked block; one-click unsubscribe works without sign-in (test).
No reply text triggers a send, a claim decision or a role change (injection tests).
An unknown delivery outcome is reconciled and never resent (test).
No outreach data appears in public, shared-party, search, federation or participant agent projections (projection tests).

packages.title: Lifecycle journeys for participants and partners inside their preferences
packages.goal: Onboarding, claimed-company onboarding, re-engagement, partner updates and notices that respect each person's notification preferences, with caps, no dark patterns and only cohort metrics.
steps: Tables lifecycle_journey, journey_step and journey_enrolment without per-person engagement fields (packages/data/migrations/lifecycle).
Journeys stop when their goal is met; re-engagement at most once per hub-set period; transactional notices only in the account and legal categories.
Templates through COMMS-001 in every hub language; no fake scarcity or fake activity wording (template lint).
acceptance: A person who turned a category off receives no journey message in it (test).
Journey metrics return cohorts only, with counts under ten suppressed (test).

packages.title: Console: discovery and outreach screens on fixtures
packages.goal: Build the outreach section (overview, policies, campaigns, templates, replies, suppression, deliverability, lifecycle journeys: HC-170 to HC-177) on fixtures with the console components.
steps: Build HC-170 to HC-177 with PolicyGateList, MessagePreview and SuppressionLookup; fixtures validated by the outreach policy contracts; synthetic data only.
Strict mode banner when outreach is off; counsel approval and second person shown before any mode change; the engine floor rendered without switches.
