packages.title: Exchange schema registry and compatibility checker
packages.goal: Register every object that crosses a node boundary as a versioned exchange schema owned by one module, generated from its Zod contract, with down-projections and a compatibility checker that runs in CI; no wire change.
steps: Define the exchange schema descriptor (identifier tw.<module>.<object>, major and minor, owner module, projection, data class, mesh kind, essential members) in packages/contracts/src/exchange-registry.ts.
Register the current mesh kinds and the commerce, content and directory payloads in packages/contracts/src/exchange-schemas with JSON Schema generated from Zod.
Implement pure down-projections to earlier minors and a checker that refuses a minor that removes, renames, retypes or tightens a member, or drops an essential member.
acceptance: A minor version that removes, renames, retypes or tightens a member fails the checker (tests).
Down-projection output validates against the earlier minor and its digest equals the digest of the same object built at that minor (tests).
A schema can never declare a projection its mesh kind does not allow (test).

packages.title: Protocol trustwork-mesh/2: contracts and conformance vectors
packages.goal: Freeze the trustwork-mesh/2 superset proposed in ADR 016 (envelope schema, language, policy and context members; new shared and public kinds; capability statement; opt-in search; new error codes) with conformance vectors. Blocked until ADR 016 is accepted.
steps: Wait for the owner and integrator decision on ADR 016; record it in the ADR.
Add the version 2 schemas in packages/contracts/src/federation-v2.ts reusing every version 1 byte rule; keep version 1 schemas unchanged.
Generate vectors in tests/federation/protocol-v2 for the new envelope members, kinds, capability statement and error codes; document the protocol in the protocol chapter.
acceptance: Every version 1 vector still verifies unchanged (test).
party_private, owner_private and staff_case are still refused by the schema; a translation with binding true is refused (tests).
Vectors are byte-reproducible and drift fails the build.

packages.title: Capability statements and per-peer exchange profiles
packages.goal: Each node signs a capability statement for its hubs; peers compute and store the same intersection (the exchange profile) and send nothing outside it.
steps: Serve the signed capability statement and fetch peers' statements on peering and on change (packages/data/migrations/federation-capabilities).
Compute the exchange profile deterministically, store it with its digest and both statement digests, and recompute on change.
Refuse outgoing and incoming deliveries outside the profile; expose an honest unavailable reason to the sending participant.
acceptance: Both nodes compute the same profile digest from the same two statements (test with two simulated nodes).
A schema outside the profile is never sent and is refused with federation.schema_unsupported when received (tests).
A profile change never alters a pinned deal; a withdrawn schema a deal needs yields federation.capability_withdrawn and a notice to both parties (test).

packages.title: Federation delivery engine: outbox, inbox processing, ordering, retries and reconciliation
packages.goal: Deliver every addressed federation item at least once with effectively-once effects: a transactional outbox, idempotent inbox processing, order inside a context, backoff, maximum age, dead letters and reconciliation of unknown outcomes by identical resend.
steps: Write federation_delivery rows in the same transaction as the business change; send from the worker with leases (apps/worker/src/federation).
Process inbox deliveries in one transaction each, with the unique (senderNode, deliveryId) constraint and the stored receipt.
Retry with backoff and jitter honouring Retry-After; move to outcome_unknown, reconcile by resending the identical body, dead-letter past the maximum age.
Apply context items in sequence order with a bounded gap hold; refuse previous-digest mismatches.
Emit cohort metrics per peer and kind only.
acceptance: A crash between commit and send never loses a delivery; a repeat never produces a second effect (fault-injection and concurrency tests).
Reconciliation never uses a new delivery identifier (test).
Metrics and logs contain no person identifiers or payloads (test).

packages.title: Usage policies: purpose, retention, residency, onward sharing and transfer bases
packages.goal: Attach a signed usage policy to every shared_party delivery and consented item, enforce purpose, retention, residency and onward sharing on the receiving node, and record a transfer basis per peering for personal data classes.
steps: Define the usage policy contract with its closed vocabulary in packages/contracts/src/exchange-policy.ts.
Evaluate the policy before storing; refuse with federation.policy_unacceptable when it cannot be honoured.
Enforce purpose at read time through the projection serializers; run retention through the privacy retention jobs; record transfer bases per peering and stop personal data classes without one.
acceptance: Data received for deal_execution never reaches search, recommendations, analytics or translation memory (negative tests).
A delivery whose residency excludes the receiving node's country is refused and nothing is stored (test).
A personal data class without a recorded transfer basis never flows to that peer (test).

packages.title: Cross-hub language negotiation and translation records
packages.goal: Carry the language of record, translation provenance and labels across nodes, produce reading translations of deal text on the reader's hub under its egress rules, and keep the original authoritative. Integrates with the translation memory package proposed by the editorial office design once it exists.
steps: Define the language block and translation record (tag, role, translationOf, method, review, binding always false) in packages/contracts/src/exchange-language.ts.

Implement reading translations for shared_party text only when the usage policy allows reading_translation and the hub egress policy allows deal_data to its provider; never store them in translation memory.
Run blocking checks (numbers, currencies, units, dates, identifiers, glossary, do-not-translate) and hide failing translations.
Record the digest of a translation shown at acceptance next to the agreement digest.
acceptance: A translation can never be marked binding and never enters an agreement digest (tests).
A translation whose numbers, units, currencies or dates differ from the original is hidden (test).
Deal text never reaches a provider without the reading hub's egress rule and never enters translation memory (negative tests).

packages.title: Cross-border commercial terms contract
packages.goal: Define the optional cross-border terms block for RFQ and quote payloads: trade terms (Incoterms 2020 rule code, version and named place), informational reference rates, tax treatment with rule sources, applicable law and dispute resolution chosen by the parties, consumer or business role, document requirements and export-control declarations.
steps: Write packages/contracts/src/cross-border.ts with strict schemas and pure validators (rule code set, sea rules need a port, rates as decimal strings with source and time, purpose informational).
Propose to the integrator the new RFQ and quote payload minor versions that embed the block; existing digests stay unchanged.
Map fields to UBL Quotation and Order elements in a documented table for exports.
acceptance: A reference rate can never be used as a settlement value (no such field; test).
A tax treatment without a rule source is refused (test).
Payloads without the block produce byte-identical digests to today's (test).

packages.title: Cross-hub agreements, orders, documents, signatures and payments
packages.goal: Carry agreements, orders, order events, e-document references and payment evidence between the parties' home nodes with the applicable-rules record, both hubs' disclosed fees, signature levels from each party's pack and payments only through licensed providers.
steps: Implement order and order_event deliveries bound to the agreement digest; budget reservation stays on the buyer's node.
Record the applicable-rules block, both fee versions shown and each party's signature level at acceptance.
Exchange e-document references with digests and fetch on demand under the usage policy; select payment providers by the cross-hub rule.
acceptance: Both nodes hold identical agreement and order digests; nothing on one node authorizes an action on the other (tests).
Acceptance is impossible until both fee versions, the applicable rules and the language of record were shown (test).
No record represents money held by a hub or by Trustwork; no currency conversion is computed (tests).

packages.title: Cross-hub disputes, appeals and moderation referrals
packages.goal: Let each hub handle its own participant's dispute and appeal while the parties assemble one evidence package from records both may see on both nodes, refer it to a mediator or the agreed forum, and record outcomes as consented evidence on each home node.
steps: Implement dispute_referral deliveries and the joint package assembly with digest verification on both nodes.
Record outcomes as consented, cited evidence on each subject's home node only.
acceptance: A hub never decides a case of the other hub's participant (test).
Packages contain only records both parties may see and verify against both nodes' digests (tests).

packages.title: Federated context threads with reading translations
packages.goal: Let parties on different nodes talk in the thread of their shared context: messages authored on each party's node, delivered as thread messages in context order, notifications created by each node for its own participant, reading translations labelled and the original one click away.
steps: Deliver thread_message items with context sequence and previous digest; store them in the context's thread on both nodes.
Create notifications per node from received messages without private values; never send to the other node's participants' external addresses.
Show reading translations from XCH-006 with labels and the original.
acceptance: Non-parties on either node get not found for the thread (negative tests).
Agent-authored messages are labelled and their text never changes state on the receiver (injection tests).
Replayed or reordered messages are refused (test).

packages.title: Passport presentation and verification across hubs
packages.goal: Let a hub verify a passport presentation issued by another hub (key chain, status list, validity, audience) and show it as verified by that hub, without importing raw reviews or recomputing reputation.
steps: Accept credential_presentation deliveries and holder-initiated presentations; verify against the issuer node's key chain at issuance time and its status list.
Display results with the issuer, evidence categories and dates; keep presentations only for the usage policy's purpose and retention.
acceptance: A revoked or expired credential is shown as such before the next display (test).
No review text or recomputed score is stored or shown from another hub (negative test).
Payment never adds, hides or reorders verified credentials (test).

packages.title: Federated public search with permission intersection
packages.goal: Offer an opt-in public query protocol between hubs that returns only public identifiers and snippets, carries no requester identity, ranks locally and inherits the intersection of source audiences.

Hydrate results from replicas or signed lookups, apply licences, rank under the local ranking statement and apply intersectReplicaAudiences.
acceptance: No private query or private context is ever sent to a peer (negative tests).
Results never include shared_party data (test).
Search is unavailable unless both hubs enable it.

packages.title: Module interop and version-skew conformance suite

Exercise each interop contract (directory, content, events, matching, procurement, sales, transactions, communications, agents, reputation) across versions.
acceptance: A deal started before an upgrade completes with identical digests on both nodes after the upgrade (test).
An essential member that would be lost by down-projection makes the feature unavailable instead of sending a lossy object (test).

packages.title: Compromised hub response, abuse controls and defederation effects
packages.goal: Detect and contain a compromised or abusive peer: revocation and equivocation handling, re-verification and hiding of affected replicas, flags on affected deals, rate limits per peer, kind and principal, and the defederation effects table, with an operator runbook.
steps: Implement equivocation detection and suspension of new signatures from the node; re-verify objects signed in the compromise window.
Apply rate limits per peer, kind and principal; dead-letter pending deliveries on defederation with notices.

acceptance: Two successors signed by the same previous key stop acceptance of the node's new signatures (test).
Accepted agreements are never voided silently; affected parties are notified (test).
Defederation stops deliveries without rewriting history (test).

packages.title: Cross-border transfer, residency and lawful-request policy for federation (counsel research)

packages.title: Cross-hub deal screens: home-hub labels, both hubs' fees, applicable rules, original and reading translation

Every label exists in every engine language; keyboard, screen reader and narrow-screen checks pass.
No screening finding, private constraint or other hub's private data appears on any screen (negative test).

Publish conformance vectors for listings and operator messages.

A network signature never verifies as a mesh signature and the reverse (tested with vectors).
Interaction settings cannot express a licence looser than the agreed term or a private projection (tested).
Published statistics accept only buckets and suppress anything below ten (tested).
No field or enum value matches FORBIDDEN_CONTROL_WORDS (tested).

packages.title: Hub directory service and listings
packages.goal: An engine directory module that accepts signed hub listings, admits them through the SANC-008 hub_directory check, mirrors other directories with re-verification and re-admission, and serves listings to admitted readers; plus the hub side that submits, refreshes and withdraws its listing.

Implement the directory module: fetch the listed node's manifest itself, verify signatures, run admitPeerAtHandshake-style admission with the hub_directory policy (declared, attested, observed), store refusal records with place and dataset only.
Implement the read endpoint with the jurisdiction gate, filters and alphabetical, distance or date order; directory-to-directory mirroring with re-verification and own admission.
acceptance: A listing whose manifest, attestation or observed place is restricted is refused with 451 and nothing about it is served (tested).
A reader in a restricted place is refused at the door (tested).
A mirrored listing is re-verified and re-admitted by the mirror, and dropped when the source withdraws it or it expires (tested).
No record holds a network address and no listing order depends on payment or statistics (tested).

packages.title: Peering requests, per-peer interaction settings, renewal, suspension and defederation handling

steps: Implement peering requests with local states and review (packages/data/migrations/federation-peer-policy).

Implement interaction settings versions in the federation configuration domain with diff, effect lines, estimated counts and second-person activation; protective (narrowing) versions apply at once with a reason.
Provide the per-peer policy port consumed by syndication, deals and federated sign-in.
Implement renewal triggers (manifest, key, attestation, licences) with automatic re-admission and suspension, and the defederation plan through the FED-002 purge-by-peer operation.
acceptance: A widening settings version cannot be activated without a second person bound to its digest; a narrowing one can be applied by one person with a reason and is shown to approvers afterwards (tested).
A looser peer manifest never loosens the agreed licences; a stricter one applies at once (tested).
An expired attestation or a refused re-admission suspends all flows in both directions (tested).
On defederation, personal-data replicas are purged within the agreed tombstone hours and shared_party deal replicas stay for the parties (tested).

packages.title: Operator channel and verified network announcements

Implement announcement pulls with verification against the project key committed in the repository, retractions and acknowledgements.
acceptance: A message carrying an address-shaped key, an IP literal or a forbidden payload key is refused (tested).
A received message or announcement never triggers an action (tested).
An unverifiable or retracted announcement is not shown as valid (tested).

packages.title: Network statistics: federation health, published hub statistics and the peering graph

Statistics never influence directory order (tested).

packages.title: Accessible world map component with an equal list view

Stories and unit tests; axe checks in the design-system suite.

The component makes no network request (tested).

Playwright and axe plans, including phone journeys.

packages.title: Console network area live wiring

steps: Implement the API adapter methods for listings, peers, requests, settings versions, messages, announcements and statistics.
Run the network browser plan against the API.

packages.title: Mobile money and instant-payment provider adapters for the launch countries
packages.goal: Let a hub configure licensed mobile-money operators, instant-payment schemes and local gateways through the payment port, each as an adapter with a deterministic fake, so hubs in Peru, the Philippines, Kenya, Ghana, Colombia, the Dominican Republic, Uzbekistan, Nigeria, Mexico and Rwanda can take payments for consultations, courses and tickets without Trustwork or the operator ever holding funds (ADR 010 decision 20).
steps: Define the adapter capability set the port needs from a provider: create a push-to-phone or QR request, receive the asynchronous callback, query status, refund where supported, pay out through the provider's licensed accounts; map provider states to the port's states including pending_customer_action and outcome_unknown.

Add a deterministic fake per provider family (mobile money push, QR code scheme, alias-based instant transfer, card gateway) with recorded fixtures of callbacks, timeouts, duplicates and reversals; no real account, key or charge.

List candidate providers per launch country as country-pack payment facts at candidate level only (for example mobile-money operators in Kenya, Ghana and Rwanda; QR Ph and e-wallet gateways in the Philippines; Yape and Plin through acquirers in Peru; Bre-B through participating providers in Colombia; SPEI in Mexico; national card schemes and licensed payment organisations in Uzbekistan; NIP gateways in Nigeria); register adapter ids in ENGINE_ADAPTERS only with a maintainer's agreement.

Refuse any configuration that routes funds through an account of the operator or the engine; refuse sanctioned banks, restricted-place payout countries and Russian rails before the provider is called.
acceptance: A push-to-phone request whose callback never arrives stays outcome_unknown until a status query reconciles it, and is never retried as a new charge (test).
Duplicate and out-of-order callbacks never double-settle (test).
No adapter credits a balance held by Trustwork or the hub operator (test and review checklist).
Every adapter runs only after a second person activates it (KEYS-001) and a synthetic test passes; fakes are labelled as fakes everywhere.

packages.title: USSD and feature-phone access to a person's own agent and tasks
packages.goal: Let people on basic phones (fundis, artisans, small suppliers) read their task and quote status, confirm a structured step and receive a claim or verification code through USSD menus and SMS, through a licensed aggregator adapter with a fake, under per-channel grants.
steps: Define a USSD session port (start, menu step, end, timeout) and an aggregator adapter with a deterministic fake; sender short codes and registration data live in hub configuration and country-pack communications facts.
Offer read-only menus (my tasks, my quotes, my confirmations) and structured confirmations that map to existing capabilities through the capability registry; free text never authorises anything.
Localise every menu in the hub languages within USSD length limits; record per-country quiet hours and opt-out keywords from the pack.
Never send marketing or outreach over USSD or SMS; only transactional messages to people who granted the channel.
acceptance: A USSD session that drops mid-confirmation leaves no commitment (test).
No menu exposes another person's private data; sessions are bound to the verified phone number of the person (negative test).
Messages go only to people who granted the channel; outreach purposes are refused on this channel (test).

packages.title: Phone-number accounts: sign-up and recovery by mobile number with SIM-swap protection
packages.goal: As a hub option, let a person sign up with a mobile number and a password instead of an e-mail address, proving possession of the number by a one-time code, because many tradespeople in the launch countries use a phone without e-mail; recovery by phone carries a cooling period and SIM-swap protection.
steps: Add a phone identifier kind alongside e-mail (E.164, country from the number), verified by a one-time code over the SMS channel adapter; the password policy and second-factor rules stay unchanged; one-time codes are never the only sign-in factor.
Responses to sign-up, sign-in and recovery stay identical whether a number exists or not; rate limits per number and per source.

Recovery by phone starts a cooling period (hub setting) during which sensitive actions are blocked and the person is notified on every other channel; a number recently ported or re-assigned (where an adapter can tell) needs extra evidence.
Let a person add an e-mail later and choose which identifier signs in; hub configuration decides whether phone accounts are offered.
acceptance: No session exists before the number is verified (test).
Sign-up and recovery responses do not reveal whether a number is registered (test).
A recovery by phone cannot change the password and payout details in the same cooling period (test).
Phone numbers never appear in public projections (negative test).

packages.title: Informal addresses and coarse public locations
packages.goal: Represent locations where streets have no names or numbers (plot and block descriptions, landmarks, national digital address codes such as GhanaPostGPS, Open Location Codes) and show public pages only coarse locations, so no active site, home or delivery address helps theft or extortion.
steps: Define an address contract with optional structured parts, a landmark description per language, an optional national digital address code (kind and pattern from the country pack) and an optional Open Location Code; coordinates are private.
Derive a public location at the precision the hub sets (district, ward or place) and never publish exact coordinates, plot numbers or digital address codes of homes and active sites.
Add country-pack address facets for digital address systems (kind, pattern, issuer, licence) at candidate level, and parsing helpers with tests.
Use OpenStreetMap data for places with ODbL attribution.
acceptance: Public projections never contain coordinates, plot numbers or digital address codes of homes or active sites (negative test).
A digital address code is validated against the pack pattern (test).
Coarsening is deterministic and documented per precision level (test).

packages.title: Informal-sector reputation path for workers and crews without a registered company
packages.goal: Let master builders, fundis, artisans and labour crews who have no registered company build and confirm reputation as people: crew profiles of named members, client confirmations of real tasks reachable by phone, and worker certificates from national training bodies presented by the holder, never sourced pages about individuals and never paid.
steps: Add a crew (group of named people with a lead, not a company) that can take tasks, with each member's consent; a crew never becomes a company page and dissolves without losing members' own records.
Let a client confirm a completed task by a link sent to the client's own verified phone or e-mail (REP-001 rules: a recorded relationship, one request plus one reminder, no incentives).

Accept worker certificates from national training bodies (for example SENCICO in Peru, TESDA in the Philippines, trade tests in Kenya, SENA in Colombia, CTVET in Ghana) as holder-presented credentials with the issuer named; verification only through the issuer's public check or an adapter; country-pack facts list issuers at candidate level.
Offline capture of evidence (photos, notes) with device and server times, synced later (CHAN-001); location stripped from public projections.
acceptance: No profile, page or score is created about a person who did not join (negative test).
A confirmation without a recorded task relationship is rejected (test).
Certificates show issuer and date and never claim verification the hub did not perform (test).
Crew membership changes never delete a member's confirmed records (test).

steps: Add phase states (planned, active, paused, resumed, done) and a horizon per phase to plan versions; a paused phase keeps its requests closed and its evidence intact.
Add "design for later" decisions (foundations and columns sized for future floors, service routes) as plan decisions that later phases inherit, with a prompt to consult a registered engineer.
Let the planner agent (AGT-010) propose phases from a goal and a budget range per period, citing guides; estimates always show sources and the word estimate.
Let a household record materials bought ahead and where they are stored (private), so later phases see them.
acceptance: A paused phase cannot receive new quotes or tasks until resumed (test).
Inherited decisions appear on every later phase with their source (test).
Plan data stays private unless the owner publishes a redacted version (negative test).

packages.title: Remote owner oversight with a delegated local representative
packages.goal: Let an owner who lives abroad, often a family member sending money home, follow a project through time-stamped evidence and milestone confirmations by a local representative acting under a limited, revocable delegation, while payments go only through licensed providers and never through the hub.
steps: Add a project delegate role bound to a structured delegation (what the delegate may confirm, until when, which milestones); the owner can revoke at any time; the delegate never gains the owner's budget authority unless the owner grants a budget.
Add evidence requests per milestone (photo sets with device and server times, short videos, receipts) and a weekly digest for the owner in the owner's language and time zone.
A milestone is accepted only by the owner or by the delegate within the delegation; chat text never accepts a milestone or instructs a payment.
Link to licensed remittance or payment providers through the payment port only (PAY-001); record references, never funds.
acceptance: A delegate cannot accept a milestone outside the delegation or after revocation (test).
Evidence shows both device and server times; location is stripped from anything shared beyond the owner (test).
No code path moves money or stores card or bank data in this module (review checklist and test).

Natural persons in registers are used only for verification evidence and never displayed publicly (negative test).

Classify works tenders with the plan-step taxonomy and hub categories; awards feed sourced track records linked by identifier only.
acceptance: No adapter submits bids or contacts buyers (test).
A publication whose licence forbids reuse cannot be activated (test).
Imported notices are labelled as public procurement notices and never appear as members' needs (test).

packages.title: Launch kits: per-country source lists and hub presets imported as proposals
packages.goal: Make a country launch repeatable and largely automatic: a reviewed, machine-readable launch kit per country (candidate sources with legal-check notes, register catalogue references, wizard presets, outreach mode default, seed-content plan by plan stage, calendar notes) that the setup wizard and the source registry import as proposals for people to approve, never as active configuration.

A kit naming a restricted place or a Russian provider fails validation (test).
Every kit source carries an evidence link and an access date (test).

packages.title: Operating function catalogue, position model and team presets

Marketing shows every promoted item labelled and the payment-neutrality locks without controls.

packages.title: Operator finance back office: the hub's own books through accounting providers
packages.goal: Keep the hub operator's own books without ever holding participants' money: ledger entry drafts from payment-provider and accounting-provider feeds through adapters with fakes, revenue records for subscriptions and credits under the accountant's policy, tax preparation packs per country pack, budgets per function and model cost forecasts.
steps: Add the operator-finance contract and an accounting provider port with a fake adapter.
Implement entry drafts, reconciliation links to BILL-002 records, revenue schedules, tax packs and budgets per function.
Let finance agent roles draft at Draft; approvals of the close and every money action stay with people.
acceptance: No code path moves money or creates a balance of participants' funds (negative tests); payout release still needs billing.release_payout_batch with a second person.
Every figure carries its source (provider reference or operator entry); unknown outcomes go to reconciliation and are never retried blindly (tested).
Tax packs are labelled as preparation for the operator's accountant, never as filings.

packages.title: People operations for hub staff: positions, recruiting coordination, onboarding, training and offboarding plans
packages.goal: Support the people who work for the hub without surveillance and without automated decisions about them: position openings, interview coordination, onboarding checklists that create ADM-004 requests a person submits, training paths per role, offboarding plans that list work and accountability to move.
steps: Add the people-ops contract in its own file with no scoring, ranking or activity fields.
Implement openings, checklists, training paths and offboarding plans with retention set by the hub's counsel-approved policy.
Let people-operations agent roles draft only.
acceptance: No field, endpoint or agent capability scores, ranks, shortlists or rejects a candidate or a staff member (schema walk and negative tests).
No activity, productivity, sentiment or last-seen measure about staff exists (schema walk).
Candidate data is deleted at the end of the configured retention (tested).

packages.title: Regional quality and standards programme
packages.goal: Help the hub raise construction quality in its region: cohort reports of disputes, defects, corrections and confirmed completions by trade, category, territory and period; a standards guides pipeline through the editorial workflow; learning programmes with partners; recognition programmes decided by a human panel and never affecting ranking.
steps: Add the quality-programme contract in its own file.
Implement cohort reports with suppression under ten and secondary suppression.
Implement recognition programmes with published criteria, panel decisions with declared conflicts and labelled results.
acceptance: No report names a company or person or shows a cohort under ten (tested with secondary suppression).
Recognition never changes ranking, matching, recommendations or reputation scores (tested) and cannot be bought.
Programme criteria changes are versioned and require a person's activation.

packages.title: Marketing and growth function: campaigns, ads policy gate and referral programmes
packages.goal: Let the hub promote itself honestly: a campaign calendar with drafts approved by people, a deterministic ads policy gate (only the hub itself is promoted, labelled, no ranking claims, no sensitive targeting, consent-bound pixels), and referral programmes whose disclosed terms are versioned and activated by a second person.
steps: Add the growth contract in its own file.
Implement campaigns, the ads policy gate and referral programme versions with fraud flags for a person to review.
Let marketing agent roles draft; send only through approved channels after a person approves.
acceptance: A campaign that sells or implies ranking, matching, reputation, verification or badges, or lacks a label, is refused by the gate (tested).
Referral rewards are the same for everyone, disclosed, and never change position (tested).
Nothing creates reviews, testimonials, follower counts or traffic (negative tests).

packages.title: Community programmes: member journeys, champions and local chapters
packages.goal: Help members succeed and lead locally: onboarding and learning journeys inside members' own preferences, champions selected by people from public evidence, and local chapters with charters, organisers bound by written rules and event kits.
steps: Add the community-programmes contract in its own file.
Implement journeys, champion programmes and chapters; stipends and event budgets are disclosed fixed amounts recorded by finance.
Let community agent roles draft only.
acceptance: Champions and organisers gain no ranking, matching or reputation advantage (tested); they are participants, never staff.
No per-member engagement score exists (schema walk); outcomes are cohorts.
Journey messages respect each member's notification preferences (tested).

packages.title: Freeze the supplier bid desk contracts
packages.goal: Freeze the contracts of the supplier bid desk (pursuits, requirements with citations, compliance matrices, library, response versions, pricing workbooks and price schedules, clarifications, teaming, reviews, submissions, outcomes and the registry entries) before any storage, with the additive changes to frozen contracts reviewed by the integrator.
steps: Zod schemas in packages/contracts/src/bid-desk/ (pursuits, requirements, library, documents, pricing, spec-checks, clarifications, teaming, reviews, outcomes, capabilities) with state machines and tests.

BidPriceScheduleSchema carries only buyer-required fields; CitationSchema requires document id, version digest and page; SubmissionRecordSchema keeps platform quote references or portal receipts with file digests.
Propose to the integrator the additive changes: ApprovalSubjectKindSchema adds bid_decision and bid_submission; agreement terms_kind adds teaming; ContextKindV2 adds pursuit.
acceptance: BidPriceScheduleSchema rejects cost, margin, floor, rate-source and note fields (schema test).
A requirement without a complete citation cannot be accepted (contract test).
Pursuit, requirement, response, workbook, clarification, teaming and submission transitions match the design states (tests).

packages.title: Pursuits, alert profiles, match explanations and bid/no-bid decisions
packages.goal: Let a supplier company follow opportunities from public notices, platform invitations, open needs and manual uploads as private pursuits, see why each matches, and decide bid or no bid for stated reasons through its approval route.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/bid-desk for pursuit, alert_profile and bid_scorecard_version; match explanations are computed per request, not stored.

Match explanations from the company's own capability profile, credentials, passport sections, declared capacity and track record against the opportunity's public data; pass, fail or unknown with evidence.
Scorecards with hard gates, company weights and cited evidence; decisions through the approval route subject kind bid_decision; an amendment flags the decision for re-confirmation.
Alerts in the same batch for every plan; deadlines in the buyer's and the person's time zones in the bid calendar.
acceptance: Pursuits, scorecards and no-bid reasons never appear in another company's projection, search or notifications (forbidden-field tests).
No endpoint returns who else follows or bids on an opportunity (negative test with two companies).
Opportunity ranking is identical with and without paid entitlements (comparison test).
No agent can record a bid decision (test).

packages.title: Tender documents, requirement extraction with citations and the compliance matrix
packages.goal: Turn untrusted tender documents into reviewed requirements, each quoted and cited to document, version and page, and keep a versioned compliance matrix that flags changes from addenda.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/bid-requirements for tender_document, bid_requirement and compliance_matrix_version.

Deterministic mapping of structured notices (eForms, OCDS); extraction of PDFs, DOCX, XLSX and scans through the PRC-005 adapter port and the model gateway under the hub egress rules; worker jobs in apps/worker/src/bid-requirements.
Quarantine of documents that appear to be another bidder's proposal or source selection material; a person decides.
Human review side by side with the cited page; addenda flag affected rows stale; pages meter.
acceptance: Text in a tender document never changes a deadline, channel, recipient, mandate or tool call (injection suite).
Every accepted requirement carries a citation with document id, version digest and page (test).
A quarantined document is never extracted or shown to the agent (test).
Company-private material reaches a model provider only under an egress allow rule (negative test).

packages.title: Content library and document builder in the buyer's formats and languages
packages.goal: Keep a current, versioned library of bid content tied to its sources of truth and assemble response versions in the buyer's outline, formats and languages with labelled translations and clean exports.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/bid-content for library_item, library_item_version, personal_content_consent, bid_response_version and export_record.
Library items read credentials (REP-001) and passport sections (PREQ-001) from their sources; owners, review cycles and expiry raise decisions waiting.
Response versions bind library item versions and drafts and freeze with a digest; translations through the translation module stay labelled until a named reviewer approves (PROV-001).

Rendering adapter with a fake in apps/worker/src/bid-documents: tagged PDF, DOCX and XLSX, buyer templates filled in place, metadata, comments, tracked changes and hidden sheets and cells removed and listed.
acceptance: A CV is inserted only with the person's recorded consent for that use (negative test).
Exports contain no author metadata, comments, tracked changes, hidden sheets or hidden cells (export test).
An expired credential cannot be inserted without a visible warning (test).
A machine-assisted translation cannot enter a frozen response version unreviewed (test).

packages.title: Pricing workbook, margin guard, price schedules and specification checks
packages.goal: Price a bid privately with sourced quantities and rates, escalation and a deterministic margin guard, send the buyer only its schedule, and check offered products against the specification.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/bid-pricing for pricing_workbook_version, bid_price_schedule, bid_security_reference and spec_check.
Workbook lines with quantity and rate sources, cost build-up in minor units, escalation from PRC-017 series, alternates and currency snapshots; data class negotiation_constraints.
Margin guard: floors, arithmetic, unbalanced pricing, coverage and consistency; deterministic, no model call.
Specification checks: exact, equivalent by rule (PRC-006), substitution proposed, missing, non-compliant, with evidence.
acceptance: A price schedule never contains a cost, margin, floor, rate source or note (schema and projection tests).
A call carrying negotiation_constraints to a model connection without an allow rule is refused (negative test).
Bid security is stored only as a provider reference; no money field can be paid through the platform (test).
Concurrent edits of a workbook version resolve with optimistic concurrency (real PostgreSQL test).

packages.title: Clarifications, deadlines and expert suggestions
packages.goal: Ask the buyer questions through the official channel before the deadline, bring answers and addenda back into the matrix, and suggest real experts through consultations when a pursuit needs advice.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/bid-clarifications for bid_clarification and addendum_link.
Channels: rfq_clarification on platform RFQs; for public notices the channel from structured notice data, sent through a channel grant or recorded after the person posts on the portal.
Deadline reminders, quiet-period refusal of meetings with the buyer, amendment acknowledgements on the checklist.
Expert suggestions with reasons, payment-blind, booked through CONS-001 with a scope chosen item by item; a conflict on the same opportunity makes the expert decline privately.
acceptance: No message is sent to an address found only in document text (test).
A clarification send requires the person's confirmation each time (test).
The requester never learns why an expert declined for a conflict (negative test).
Expert suggestions are identical with and without paid entitlements and commissions (comparison test).

packages.title: Teaming and subcontractor sourcing with the anti-collusion guard
packages.goal: Find partners for gaps, share only their scope, receive their quotes privately and bind teaming agreements by both parties' confirmation after screening, with a guard against collusion and competitor signals.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/bid-teaming for partner_request, scope_package and competition_note_acknowledgement; teaming agreements as COM-002 agreements with terms_kind teaming once the integrator accepts it.
Partner candidates through MATCH-001 introductions within quota; scope packages limited to the partner's requirements, files and dates.
Potential-competitor teaming shows the hub's competition-law note and requires a recorded reason; exclusivity clauses flagged.
Guard: block attaching workbooks to partner threads; warn on own totals, margins or strategy in partner messages; screening gate before binding.
acceptance: A teaming agreement with a party that is matched, held, unscreened, stale or unreadable in screening is refused (gate test, fails closed).
A subcontractor never sees which primes or other subcontractors take part; a prime sees only its own sub-quotes (negative tests).
A workbook cannot be attached to a partner thread (test).

packages.title: Review rounds, approvals, the submission checklist and the human submission step
packages.goal: Review and approve bids against bound versions, compute a submission checklist that blocks on failures, and let only a person submit: on the platform as a digest-bound quote version, on an official portal by the person with a recorded receipt.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/bid-submissions for review_round, review_comment, submission_checklist and submission_record.
Review rounds bind response and workbook digests; approval route subject kind bid_submission; segregation of duties between the price writer and the approver above a company threshold.
Checklist from the matrix, outline, margin guard, pack facts and screening state; failures block.

Platform submission through COM-002 send_quote with person_each_step_up; portal submission recorded with receipt and file digests compared with the frozen export; unknown outcomes go to reconciliation.
acceptance: No mandate, extension or connection can submit, record a portal submission or withdraw a bid without step-up confirmation (test over every approval policy).
A new response or workbook version supersedes pending reviews and approvals (test).
Concurrent confirmations of the same submission resolve once (real PostgreSQL test).
The desk stores no portal credentials (configuration test).

packages.title: Outcomes, debriefs, lessons, awards as sourced history and hand-off to execution
packages.goal: Record outcomes, track debrief and standstill windows from pack facts, keep lessons, turn public awards into sourced track record and hand wins to execution.
steps: Migrations in packages/data/migrations/bid-outcomes for bid_outcome, debrief_record, lesson and external_contract_record.
Outcomes from PRC-004 notices, PROC-001 awards linked by identifier, or a person's record with evidence.
Debrief request drafts through the official channel; lessons linked to library items; company-level metrics with a self-view.
Hand-off: platform agreements to EXE-001; off-platform contracts to a private external contract record with obligations drafted into a company project.
acceptance: An award linked by name only is rejected (test).
A public award appears as a sourced portfolio line, never as a client confirmation (test).
No metric is computed per person for a viewer other than that person (test).

packages.title: Bid desk entries in the shared capability registry (agent parity)
packages.goal: Apply ADR 010 decision 23 to the bid desk: every operation is one registry entry used by the agent runtime, MCP connections and the interface, and the CI parity report shows no gap.
steps: Register the entries of packages/contracts/src/bid-desk/capabilities.ts; until the engine-wide registry runtime exists (MCP-001), serve them from this module behind the same interface.
Bind each capability to one use case; the web route and the agent tool call the same use case.
govern entries are never exposed to MCP or A2A; person_each_step_up commits cannot be confirmed by a connection.
acceptance: A parity test fails when a capability lacks a web route or an agent tool, or when a route or tool lacks a capability (test).
Only reads and drafts accept untrusted text (registry invariant test).

packages.title: Bid desk agent module for suppliers
packages.goal: Ship the bid_desk agent module so a supplier's one agent can watch and qualify opportunities, draft scorecards, extract requirements, draft sections and translations, check specifications and prices, draft questions, find partners, prepare reviews and the checklist, and track outcomes, all within mandates, with submission and decisions left to people.
steps: Module manifest with jobs, triggers, mandate templates, meters and locale keys for every engine language; only registry capabilities of BID-009 and CONS-001.
Refuse collusive goals and mandates with the hub's competition-law note; repeated attempts open a case for a person.

Safety suite on the EVAL-001 harness: injected instructions in tender documents and addenda, deadline and channel spoofing, price and margin disclosure to partners and buyers, competitor-information requests, submission through chat text, consultation booking without confirmation.
acceptance: The module cannot submit, withdraw, accept a teaming agreement, decide bid or no bid or approve a review (tests).
Workbook data never appears in an outbound message or a model call without an egress allow rule (tests).
Every safety scenario produces no external effect without a valid mandate and the person's confirmation (suite).

packages.title: Bid desk on the web: dashboard, opportunities, bid/no-bid, compliance matrix, library and document builder
packages.goal: Build the first half of the supplier bid desk screens under Sales on the API, following the screen contract, with every action mapped to a registry capability.
steps: Routes under apps/web/app/app/sales/tenders for the dashboard, opportunities, library and the pursuit overview, requirements and documents tabs; components in apps/web/components/bid-desk.
Strings in a bid-desk namespace in every engine language; dates, numbers and money through Intl.
Playwright and axe at three widths with two companies to prove isolation.
acceptance: No screen shows how many companies follow or bid on an opportunity (browser test).
Citations open the cited page; agent drafts and machine translations are labelled (browser tests).
Keyboard, screen reader, 375 px, empty, error, denied and offline states verified.
Every screen action maps to a capability of the parity registry (test).

packages.title: Bid desk on the web: pricing workbook, clarifications, team, reviews, submission and outcomes
packages.goal: Complete the supplier bid desk screens: pricing with the margin guard, questions, team and partners, reviews and approvals, the submission checklist with the person's confirmation, and outcomes.
steps: Pursuit tabs pricing, clarifications, team, reviews, submission and outcome, and the outcomes list, as sub-routes of the WEB-013 tenders routes; strings added to the bid-desk namespace in every engine language.
Submission confirmation names the recipient, the files' digests and the deadline before step-up; portal submissions are recorded with the receipt.
Playwright journeys at three widths in a non-English language.
acceptance: The pricing tab never renders for a member without the pricing right, and the buyer preview shows no cost or margin (browser tests).
Submitting requires the first-party confirmation with step-up; chat text in the assistant never submits (browser test).
Keyboard, screen reader and 375 px checks pass on the workbook with the wide-screen hint.

packages.title: Public procurement facets for bid desks in country packs
packages.goal: Let the bid desk read every country-specific procurement rule from packs and layers: notice standards, supplier registrations, self-declaration forms, submission rules, bid security, debrief and standstill windows, integrity forms, automated-access terms, record retention and classification schemes.
steps: Add the fact types as an additive schema module in packages/country-packs/src/procurement-facts.ts referenced by the procurement facet, with validation tests in tests/country-packs/procurement.

Source the United States facts (SAM.gov registration and terms, FAR debrief, bid guarantee and bond rules, record retention, NAICS and PSC) and the EU layer facts (eForms, ESPD and eCertis, standstill, CPV) from official sources with verification levels, in a data file per scope under packages/country-packs/procurement.
Leave UK and other national facts to their pack packages; record South Africa (eTenders OCDS and CSD) as a candidate example only.
acceptance: Every fact cites an official source with retrieval date and verification level; secondary-only facts stay pending (validation test).
The engine reads these facts without any country branch in code (test with a synthetic pack).

packages.title: Shared administrative shell and responsive navigation compositions
packages.goal: Compose the existing accessible primitives into the proposed console shell without duplicating domain authority.
steps: Build shared shell, header, contextual navigation and responsive menu compositions using existing tokens and primitives.
Preserve one avatar, one participant company and one assistant; staff scope switches never impersonate participants.
Provide seven-language messages, keyboard stories and narrow-screen evidence.
acceptance: All seven languages fit at 375 and 1280 px without whole-document overflow.
Menu and palette focus returns correctly; landmarks and current location are announced.
No root dependency, hard-coded brand, domain permission or new authorization path is introduced.

packages.title: Shared administrative review and recovery compositions
packages.goal: Give console domains reusable loading, forbidden, second-person review and unknown-outcome states with unchanged authority semantics.
steps: Compose existing review, reason, audit and approval primitives into operational state layouts.
Keep saving, requesting approval, activation and reconciliation distinct.
Provide locale-complete examples and keyboard, status-announcement and focus tests.
acceptance: Unknown outcomes never render as success or encourage a blind retry.
Unavailable and forbidden states reveal no private object fields.
Second-person, stale-digest and required-reason states remain usable by keyboard at 375 px in every language.

packages.title: Apply the administrative shell to the existing console
packages.goal: Apply the reviewed shell compositions to the existing administrative routes while preserving their data adapters and permission checks.
steps: Replace the console shell and responsive navigation presentation using DS-005 and HUBC-020.
Preserve deep links, real versus fixture mode, scoped staff identity, the account menu and all existing domain routes.
Add dedicated seven-language shell copy and focused keyboard, mobile, no-impersonation and denied-scope regression evidence.
acceptance: Existing routes and deep links remain reachable with the same authorization and data adapter.
All seven locales fit at 375 and 1280 px; keyboard menu/palette and focus restoration pass.
One avatar and no participant agent-management or company-switcher surface is introduced.

packages.title: Integrate administrative review journeys and acceptance evidence
packages.goal: Integrate shared operational journeys across completed domain screens without replacing their domain authority or API adapters.
steps: Add shared journey compositions and integration evidence for completed domain routes, coordinating any owning-route edits in their issues.
Carry reason, current digest, second-person, private-denial and unknown-outcome states through actual API-backed flows.
Record seven-language responsive, keyboard and human accessibility review evidence; preserve unfinished domain status.
acceptance: A domain integration cannot turn fixture-only or unavailable behavior into a live acceptance claim.
Negative authorization, stale-digest, self-approval and concurrent-decision tests cover each adopted authority flow.
Every integrated journey has non-English phone screenshots and explicit native-language and screen-reader review status.
